2. A helper for this already exists but is never called: `_make_entry(value, prev=None)` at backend.py:564-566. It also falls back to 0 instead of None when there is no previous value, so it needs fixing too.
3. Only the header is affected. The other places that show these series (App.jsx:4066-4068 for the 10Y and DXY rows, and the `C()` helper at 3724-3726, which sets pct to null for macro data) already hide the change. That narrows the blast radius.
4. Severity: the levels (VIX 24.10, 10Y 4.12%, DXY) are correct. Only the small change figure is fabricated, and it reads +0.00 every single day, so an attentive user can spot it. Nobody would size a trade off a header delta. It is misleading, but by the rubric it is medium, not high.
5. The staleness point is right for FRED: DGS10 and DGS2 appear with roughly a one-business-day lag, so the header can show the day-before-yesterday's close with no label. The CBOE VIX_History.csv is end-of-day. The Stooq daily CSV can include today's partial bar, so it is not strictly end-of-day. Either way, a missing as_of date is a real gap.
6. Small addition: showing the 10Y change as a bare `toFixed(2)` in percentage points is ambiguous. Rate moves are quoted in basis points.
findings.corrected_fix:
Backend (backend.py):
(a) Change `_fred_rate` (518-531), `_cboe_vix` (534-547) and `_stooq_dxy` (550-561) so each returns a tuple `(as_of, last, prev)`, taken from the last two valid rows:
- Keep reading from the bottom, collect valid rows until you have two, and keep `parts[0]` as the date.
- FRED: skip rows whose value is "." or empty.
- CBOE: column 4 is CLOSE; the date is in MM/DD/YYYY format, so normalize it to ISO.
- Stooq: the date is column 0 and the close is column 4.
- If only one valid row exists, `prev` is None.

(b) Fix the unused `_make_entry` (564-566) and use it for every series:
`def _make_entry(value, prev=None, as_of=None, bp=False): chg = round(value - prev, 4) if prev is not None else None; e = {"value": round(value, 4), "change": chg, "change_pct": round(chg / prev * 100, 2) if chg is not None and prev else None, "as_of": as_of}; if bp: e["change_bp"] = round(chg * 100, 1) if chg is not None else None; return e`

(c) In `_get_macro_fresh`, replace lines 575, 587 and 589 with `_make_entry(last, prev, as_of, bp=True)` for DGS10 and DGS2, and `_make_entry(last, prev, as_of)` for VIX and DXY.

(d) In `_bulk_download` (lines 664-668 and 682-686), when `len < 2`, set `prev = None` so the change becomes None instead of 0. Also add `as_of = col.index[-1].date().isoformat()`.

Frontend (App.jsx:2240-2248):
- Render the change only when `typeof m.chg === "number"`.
- For the 10Y, show `change_bp` with a "pb" suffix, e.g. "+4 pb", instead of `chg.toFixed(2)`.
- When the change is exactly 0, show it in the muted color, not green.
- Show `as_of` as a small label or tooltip, e.g. "10Y 4.12% · cierre 19-sep", at least whenever `as_of` is not today's date in America/Mexico_City. Mention that FRED data lags by about one business day.

Optional: the same `change_bp` field could be shown in the 10Y and DXY rows at App.jsx:4066-4068, which currently pass `pct={null}`.

Do not replace the zeros with the Yahoo `marketData.vix/dxy/t10y` changes. Those come from a different source and timestamp than the displayed FRED, CBOE and Stooq levels, so the level and the change would not match.

findings.title: The 'LIVE' badge, today's date and 'Act. HH:MM' imply real-time data, but quotes are delayed Yahoo daily bars that show the previous session before the open, at weekends and on holidays
findings.evidence: ResumenManero renders today = new Date().toLocaleDateString(...) and LIVE. The hero shows 'Act. {lastUpdStr}', where lastUpdated = new Date() at fetch time (1941). Backend: val = float(col.iloc[-1]); prev = float(col.iloc[-2]); results[key] = {"value":..., "change":..., "change_pct":...}, with no bar date.
findings.why: At 7am Mexico City (a 'Resumen Mañanero') or on a Saturday, 'S&P 500 sube 1.2%' is Friday's or yesterday's move, shown under today's date with a pulsing LIVE badge. On a BMV holiday the IPC line repeats the last session's move. BTC and Asian indices on the same card are for the current day, so one summary mixes different as-of dates. 'Act. HH:MM' is when the browser fetched, not when the data was observed. Yahoo quotes are also delayed for many exchanges. Presenting stale data as current breaks a basic rule of market-data display (always show quote time and delay).
findings.fix: In _bulk_download, add as_of = col.index[-1].isoformat() and prev_date = col.index[-2].isoformat(). In the UI, compare as_of with today in the exchange's time zone. Show 'Cierre vie 19-sep' when they differ, and 'Con retraso' during the session. Replace LIVE with 'Retraso ~15 min' / 'Al cierre'. Mark the Resumen lines whose data is from the previous session, e.g. 'S&P 500 cerró ayer +1.2%'.
findings.verify_reasoning: I checked every cited line. The core claim holds. One detail is wrong, and the finding misses some evidence that makes it stronger. What the code does: - App.jsx 633-638: ResumenManero sets `today = new Date().toLocaleDateString("es-MX", {weekday:"long",...})`. Line 708 renders a pulsing `LIVE`. Line 711 shows `{today}` under the title. - The summary lines use the present tense: "Bolsa mexicana avanza/retrocede X%" (644-645), "S&P 500 sube/baja X% ... Wall Street en verde/en rojo" (649-650), and "Oro avanza" (672). - App.jsx 1936-1943: loadMarketData calls `setLastUpdated(new Date())` right after fetch. Lines 3740-3742 format it, and line 3811 shows "· Act. {lastUpdStr}". So "Act." is the browser's fetch time. It is not when the data was observed. The backend also caches /market for 120 s (backend.py 702-704, `_cached("market", ..., ttl=120)`), so the data can be older still. - backend.py 644-668: `_bulk_download` calls `yf.download(syms, period="5d", interval="1d")`. For each symbol it takes `col = closes[sym].dropna()`, `val = col.iloc[-1]`, `prev = col.iloc[-2]`, and returns only `{value, change, change_pct}`, with no bar date. The fallback at 677-685 does the same. Before the open, at weekends and on holidays, `iloc[-1]` is the last completed session. On a BMV holiday while the US is open, `dropna()` drops the NaN ^MXX row, so the IPC line shows the last session's move again. During the session, the daily bar is a partial bar from Yahoo, which is delayed for many exchanges. - No disclaimer exists anywhere. A grep for "retraso|delayed|diferido|15 min|tiempo real|al cierre|as_of" finds nothing in App.jsx or ui.jsx. The numbers are correct for their own dates. The problem is labeling: present-tense verbs, today's date and a LIVE badge make old moves look current. On a Saturday the card says "S&P 500 sube 1.2%" about Friday. That is materially misleading, so high severity is defensible, although no value is actually wrong. Market-data display convention is to show each quote's time and delay status. What the finding gets wrong: - It says "BTC and Asian indices on the same card". ResumenManero has no Nikkei or HSI line. Those are only in `_MARKET_SYMS` and the Panorama panels. - The mixing on the card is actually broader than claimed. At 7am Mexico City, BTC-USD (24/7, UTC day), GC=F and CL=F (nearly 24h futures) and USDMXN=X (24/5) all show today's partial bar. IPC and S&P show the previous close. What the finding misses: - The VIX and 10Y lines on the same card (655-666) come from `get_macro`. VIX is read from CBOE's daily VIX_History.csv (backend.py 534-547), so it is always a previous-day close. The 10Y and 2Y come from FRED DGS10/DGS2 (516-531, 571-584). FRED publishes these with about a one-business-day lag. Both parsers throw away the date column (`parts[0]`). So even during the session, the "LIVE" card mixes intraday S&P with yesterday's VIX and a 10Y that can be two days old. - The same LIVE badge plus "Datos en vivo ... conectados al backend real" also appears on the login screen (App.jsx 977, 985). Where the fix needs correcting: - A daily-bar date alone cannot tell "partial bar during the session" from "today's close after the session". Both give `as_of == today`. You also need exchange hours. - `yf.download` with several tickers returns a tz-naive daily index, while `Ticker.history` in the fallback returns a tz-aware one. Normalize both to a date. - The macro sources need dates too.
findings.corrected_fix:
1) backend.py `_bulk_download`, both paths:
- Add `as_of = pd.Timestamp(col.index[-1]).date().isoformat()` and `prev_as_of = pd.Timestamp(col.index[-2]).date().isoformat()`. In the fallback, also apply `dropna()` to `hist["Close"]`.
- Return them with each entry: `{value, change, change_pct, as_of, prev_as_of}`.
- In `_get_market_fresh`, add a top-level `fetched_at` (UTC ISO timestamp) so the UI can show when the backend actually got the data, not when the browser fetched from the 120 s cache.

2) backend.py macro:
- Make `_fred_rate` return `(value, parts[0])`, and do the same in `_cboe_vix` and `_stooq_dxy`.
- Put `as_of` into the t10y, t2y, vix and dxy entries.
- Only compute the spread when t10y and t2y have the same date. Otherwise return spread with both dates.

3) Frontend helper `quoteStatus(key, entry)`:
- Keep a small map from symbol to exchange time zone and regular hours:
  - ^MXX: America/Mexico_City, 08:30-15:00
  - ^GSPC/^IXIC/^DJI: America/New_York, 09:30-16:00
  - ^N225, ^HSI, European indices: their local zones
  - Futures, FX and crypto: flagged as 24h
- Compute `todayLocal` in that zone.
  - If `as_of < todayLocal`: "Cierre {vie 19-sep}".
  - If `as_of == todayLocal` and the session is open: "Con retraso (~15-20 min)".
  - If `as_of == todayLocal` and the session has closed: "Cierre de hoy".
  - For 24h instruments: "24h · corte {as_of}".
- For macro: "VIX cierre {as_of}" and "10Y (FRED) {as_of}".

4) ResumenManero (App.jsx 633-711):
- Replace the LIVE badge with a neutral badge: "Datos con retraso", or "Al cierre" when every equity line is from before today.
- Keep today's date in the header, and add a subtitle such as "Cifras al cierre del {fecha}" when they differ.
- Pick the verb tense from the status. For previous sessions use the past tense with the date, e.g. "S&P 500 cerró +1.2% el vie 19-sep" and "Bolsa mexicana cerró −0.4%". Use "sube"/"avanza" only when the bar is from today's open session.
- Add a short as-of tag to each line, especially VIX and 10Y.

5) Hero (App.jsx 3740-3742, 3811): replace "Act. {lastUpdStr}" with "Datos: {hora de fetched_at} · Yahoo Finance, con retraso". Show per-quote as-of or status in DataRow.

6) Login screen (App.jsx 977, 985): remove the LIVE badge, or relabel it, and change "Datos en vivo" to "Datos de mercado con retraso".

findings.title: VIX, 10Y and DXY are shown twice on the same screen from different sources, with different values
findings.evidence: The Indicadores Principales grid calls C(key, dec, macro) with macro undefined for 'vix','dxy','t10y', so it reads md (Yahoo ^VIX, DX-Y.NYB, ^TNX from /market). Fear & Greed and the Resumen use macroData.vix (CBOE prior close). The México panel shows macroData.t10y (FRED DGS10, T-1) and macroData.dxy (Stooq 'dxy.fo'). The header strip also uses macroData.
findings.why: A terminal should have one number per instrument. Users will see, for example, VIX 18.9 in one tile and 17.6 in the gauge, and 10Y 4.31% vs 4.27% a few centimetres apart. That undermines trust, and the gauge ends up computed from a different value than the one displayed. Mixing an intraday ^TNX with a T-1 DGS2 in the fallback path also produces a spread from two different dates.
findings.fix: Choose one canonical source per instrument, with a documented fallback order, and give every consumer the same object. Suggested: /market's Yahoo quote, with as_of, for intraday display of VIX/DXY/10Y; FRED only for curve points not on Yahoo (2Y), with its date shown. Or merge /macro into /market so the frontend never has to pick between two sources.
findings.verify_reasoning:
I checked the finding against the code and it holds. A few details need tightening.

1. **Two sources.** In /Users/luisalfredolizarragasanchez/Desktop/CLAUDE/05 NEWKAIZEN/src/App.jsx:3724-3727, the news tab defines `C = (k, dec, macro) => { const d = macro ? macroData?.[k] : md?.[k]; ... }`. None of the entries in the Indicadores Principales array (3887-3896) sets `macro`, so the VIX, DXY and 10Y tiles read `marketData`. That comes from `${BACKEND}/market` (1939), which the backend maps to `"vix":"^VIX","dxy":"DX-Y.NYB","t10y":"^TNX"` (backend.py:638) through `_bulk_download`. That call returns the latest daily bar, which is intraday during the session, plus `change_pct`.

2. **Every other consumer reads `macroData`.** It comes from `${BACKEND}/macro` (1236), built in backend.py:569-622:
   - 10Y is FRED `DGS10` (T-1, constant maturity).
   - VIX is the last row of CBOE `VIX_History.csv` (the prior close while the market is open).
   - DXY is the last close from Stooq.

   The consumers that read it:
   - Header strip (2240-2243), on every tab.
   - ResumenManero (658-668, rendered at 3879 with `macroData`).
   - The `vixVal` behind the Fear & Greed gauge (3745, 3986-4018).
   - The México · Mercado panel rows (4065-4068).

   So on the news tab VIX appears four times from two sources, 10Y four times from two sources, and DXY three times from two sources. The two feeds measure slightly different things. `^TNX` is an on-the-run yield and DGS10 a constant-maturity par yield from the day before, so a few bp apart is normal. For VIX, intraday vs the prior close can differ by several points on volatile days.

3. **Worse than claimed: the gap grows.** `macroData` is fetched once on mount (1232-1238) and never refreshed. `marketData` refreshes every 60 s (1976). The longer the session, the further apart the numbers drift. Also, every `/macro` entry hard-codes `"change": 0` (backend.py:575, 587, 589), and the header strip renders `m.chg` whenever it is not null (2240-2243). The header therefore always shows a green "+0.00" for VIX, DXY and 10Y, while the Indicadores tile a few centimetres away shows a real `change_pct`.

4. **The mixed-date fallback is real but an edge case.** If FRED DGS10 fails and DGS2 succeeds, `t10y` falls back to Yahoo `^TNX` (594-601). The spread (613-618) then subtracts a T-1 DGS2 from a live `^TNX`. Both series come from the same FRED endpoint, so this is unlikely but possible. The comment at 617, which says both values come from FRED, is then false.

**Details to correct:**
- The gauge prints the same `vixVal` it was computed from (line 4018), so it is consistent with itself. The mismatch is between the gauge and the Indicadores VIX tile.
- The proposed fix, "Yahoo for 10Y display, FRED for 2Y", would recreate the mixed-date spread the finding criticises, unless the spread comes from a same-date FRED source.
- The backend deliberately makes FRED and CBOE primary because Yahoo is rate-limited from Render (comments at 572 and 591). Making Yahoo the only canonical source would make things less reliable, not more.

Severity medium is appropriate: the gaps are small, but they are visible and undermine trust. This is not critical.
findings.corrected_fix:
1. **Backend (backend.py).** Build one canonical quote per instrument in `_get_macro_fresh`, or merge it into `/market`, with this shape:
   `{value, change, change_pct, as_of, source}`
   - VIX, DXY and 10Y level: take the Yahoo bar from the cached `get_market()` (^VIX, DX-Y.NYB, ^TNX). Fall back to CBOE, then Stooq, then FRED DGS10.
   - When a fallback is used, compute the real change from the last two CSV rows instead of the hard-coded 0 at lines 575, 587 and 589, and return that row's date as `as_of`.
   - Change `_fred_rate`, `_cboe_vix` and `_stooq_dxy` to return `(date, value, prev_value)`.

2. **Curve spread.** Compute it only from same-date data. Use FRED `T10Y2Y`, or DGS10 and DGS2 aligned on the same date (drop rows where either is "."). Expose it as `spread: {value_bp, as_of}`. Never subtract a FRED 2Y from a Yahoo 10Y. If DGS10 is missing, set spread to null instead of pairing it with ^TNX. Label it in the UI as "Spread 10Y–2Y (FRED, dd-mmm)".

3. **Frontend (src/App.jsx).** Use one accessor everywhere:
   `const q = k => marketData?.[k] ?? macroData?.[k]`
   Pass it, or a merged object, to every consumer:
   - Indicadores grid (3887-3897)
   - ResumenManero (658-668)
   - `vixVal` for the Fear & Greed gauge (3745)
   - México panel rows (4065-4068), which should drop the duplicate 10Y and DXY rows or show `q(k).change_pct`
   - Header strip (2240-2243)
   Only render `chg` when the source actually provides it.

4. **Refresh.** Refresh `/macro` on the same interval as `/market` (next to line 1976), or retire it once it is merged. The two can then no longer drift apart during a session.

5. **Freshness labels.** Show a small freshness tag for any value that is not intraday, e.g. "cierre 19-sep" or "FRED T-1", so users know which values are delayed.

findings.title: US 10Y change is shown as a percent of the yield, not in basis points
findings.evidence: { key: "t10y", label: "US 10Y Treasury", dec: 2, unit: "%" } takes pct from md.t10y.change_pct, which the backend computes as (chg / prev) * 100 on ^TNX. It is rendered as {up ? "+" : ""}{Math.abs(d.pct).toFixed(2)}%.
findings.why: Yield moves are quoted in basis points. A 5 bp rise from 4.00% to 4.05% displays as '+1.25%', which reads like a 1.25-point rate jump or gets confused with price returns. The Resumen already quotes the spread correctly in 'pb', so the page is internally inconsistent.
findings.fix: For yield instruments (t10y, and t2y/spread if added), display change*100 rounded as '+5 pb' and drop change_pct. Add a flag such as kind:'yield' in _MARKET_SYMS metadata so the frontend picks the right format.
findings.verify_reasoning:
The finding holds up against the code.

1. Where the number comes from. The market t10y value is built in backend.py. _MARKET_SYMS (line 638) maps "t10y" to "^TNX". _bulk_download (lines 666-668) computes chg = val - prev and change_pct = (chg / prev) * 100, and the fallback at lines 684-686 does the same. So change_pct is the yield's move as a percent of the yield itself, not a move in basis points.

2. How it is shown. In src/App.jsx, the helper C at lines 3724-3727 returns { value, pct: d?.change_pct, abs: d?.change } from marketData, which is loaded from /market at line 1939. The card at line 3894 ({ key: "t10y", ..., unit: "%" }) prints the level as fv(value) + "%". The change is printed at lines 3915-3919 as {up ? "+" : ""}{Math.abs(d.pct).toFixed(2)}%.
   - Example: a move from 4.00 to 4.05 shows "+1.25%". The market convention is "+5 pb".
   - Because the level sits right next to it with a "%" sign, "+1.25%" reads as a 1.25-point rate jump.
   - Line 668 (in ResumenManero) already quotes the spread in "pb", so the page does contradict itself.
   - This is the only place market t10y is used (grep finds only line 3894), so nothing else relies on change_pct for t10y.

3. Nothing else fixes it. No other code path rescales this value.

Details the finding misses:
- (a) No backend change or metadata flag is needed. C already exposes abs (d.change, in percentage points, rounded to 4 decimals), and the card config at line 3894 is the natural place for a flag. Also, _MARKET_SYMS is a plain key-to-symbol dict that gets inverted at line 699, so putting metadata there would mean restructuring it.
- (b) Scale. Yahoo's ^TNX now quotes the yield directly (for example 4.05), so bp = change * 100. The old CBOE convention quoted TNX at 10x the yield (40.5), where bp would be change * 10. A cheap guard is worth adding. change_pct gives the same wrong number under either scale.
- (c) Color. The card colors a rising yield green and a falling one red (up = pct >= 0, then var(--positive)). A rising yield means falling bond prices, so green-for-up is misleading. Neutral colors, or colors from a bondholder's point of view, would be better.
- (d) The header strip has related problems:
  - Line 2243 shows the 10Y from FRED with chg: macroData.t10y?.change. _fred_entry (backend.py lines 573-574) hard-codes change to 0, so the strip always shows "+0.00".
  - Line 2241 shows the spread as a bare "+0.52" with no unit.
  - The same page mixes ^TNX (live, on the card) with FRED DGS10 (prior-day close, in the strip and Resumen), so the two 10Y levels can differ.

Severity: medium is right. The number is misleading and inconsistent, but the yield level itself is correct.
findings.corrected_fix:
Do the fix in the frontend. No backend change is needed.

1. At src/App.jsx line 3894, change the entry to { key: "t10y", label: "US 10Y Treasury", dec: 2, unit: "%", bp: true } and add bp to the destructuring in the .map.

2. In the change span at lines 3915-3919, branch on bp. Use d.abs, which C already returns as change in percentage points:
   const bps = d.abs == null ? null : Math.round(d.abs * (d.value > 20 ? 10 : 100));
   (The 20 cutoff guards against the old 10x ^TNX scale.)
   Render {bps > 0 ? "+" : ""}{bps} pb.
   Base isN and up on d.abs for this card, not d.pct.
   For color, use a neutral color, or invert it (rising yield = var(--negative) from a bondholder's point of view). Don't color it green just because it went up.

3. Optionally, in backend.py _bulk_download, return change_bp for yield symbols (^TNX, ^IRX) and send change_pct: None for them, so no other consumer can show the misleading percent.

4. Related fixes in the header strip:
   - Line 2243: macroData.t10y.change always comes from FRED as 0 (backend.py line 574). Either compute a real change in _fred_entry (fetch the last two DGS10 observations and store (v - prev) * 100 as change_bp), or hide chg when it is 0 or not available.
   - Line 2241: show the spread as `${Math.round(spread * 100)} pb`, matching Resumen at line 668.

5. Take the 10Y level from one source for the whole page, or label the FRED value as the prior close, so the card and the strip don't show different levels.

findings.title: USD/MXN rising (peso weakening) is coloured green in three panels and red in the Resumen
findings.evidence: Bento: const up = d?.change_pct >= 0; badgeBg = ... up ? "#79df9b" ... DataRow: const cc = up ? "var(--positive)" : "var(--negative)". Resumen: color: up ? "var(--negative)" : "var(--positive)" with the text 'Peso se debilita'.
findings.why: USD/MXN is quoted as MXN per USD, so a rise means the peso depreciated. For the target user (MXN base currency, MXN-denominated spending) that is a loss of purchasing power, yet three widgets show it as good news while the Resumen shows it as bad. The same applies to EUR/MXN. Inconsistent colour meaning makes the dashboard harder to read at a glance.
findings.fix: Colour FX pairs neutrally (sign plus arrow, no green/red), or colour USD/MXN and EUR/MXN from the peso's point of view in every widget, and add a sub-label 'Peso −0.45%' / '↑ = peso más débil'. Apply the rule through one helper so all widgets agree.
findings.verify_reasoning:
The inconsistency is real. I checked it in src/App.jsx:
- Resumen (653-656): `color: up ? "var(--negative)" : "var(--positive)"` with the text "Peso se debilita / se fortalece". So USD/MXN going up shows red.
- Bento (3842, 3848-3852): the usdmxn card is the light variant (bg #79df9b, fg #11251c), so `isDark` is false. When the pair rises the badge is dark "#11251c", not green. When it falls the badge is red var(--negative). The finding calls the rise "green", which is wrong in detail, but the meaning is the same: up is not red and down is red.
- Indicadores Principales (3895-3900, drawn at 3916): `cc = up ? "var(--positive)" : "var(--negative)"`, so a rise is green.
- México · Mercado panel (4055-4056, through DataRow 3749-3752): the same green-up rule for USD/MXN and EUR/MXN.
So one screen gives the same number two opposite colour meanings. That is a real readability problem.

Where the finding goes wrong:
1) The "why" says three widgets show a peso loss "as good news". That misreads them. Those widgets use price-direction colouring (green means the quoted price rose), which is the normal convention in Bloomberg and Refinitiv style terminals, and they apply it to every row the same way. The odd one out is the Resumen, which switches to economic-sentiment colouring.
2) The economics claim that a rising USD/MXN is plainly bad for the target user is misapplied. This app is built for Mexicans who hold US stocks (the portfolio converts USD holdings with USDMXN_SPOT, lines 123-137). For them a weaker peso raises the MXN value of those holdings. It only hurts their MXN purchasing power for imports and USD costs. There is no single good direction, so fixing the whole dashboard to the peso's point of view (one of the two fixes offered) would build in a questionable judgement.
3) The problem is wider than cited. DXY is coloured green-up in the top macro strip (line 2242, colour at 2249) and in Indicadores (line 3894). Its meaning is just as ambiguous.
Medium severity is reasonable to slightly high. No numbers are wrong, and the finding itself says it only makes the dashboard harder to read at a glance, so low-to-medium also fits.
findings.corrected_fix:
Use one colour meaning everywhere: price direction, the terminal convention. Do not use a "peso point of view".
(1) Add one helper near fv(), for example `const chgColor = (pct) => pct == null ? "var(--muted)" : pct >= 0 ? "var(--positive)" : "var(--negative)"`. Use it in DataRow (3751), in the Indicadores grid (3898) and in the macro strip (2249). In the Bento badge, keep the existing up/down palette.
(2) In ResumenManero line 655, stop flipping the colour. Either use `chgColor(md.usdmxn.change_pct)`, or use a neutral tone such as var(--warning) or var(--muted) for the FX line. Keep the explanatory text "Peso se debilita X% — dólar en $…".
(3) Help the reader: give USD/MXN and EUR/MXN a sub-label "↑ = peso más débil". Put it in the `sub` field at 4055-4056 and add it to the Indicadores/Bento labels. Optionally show the peso's own move as a secondary figure, for example "Peso −0.45%", computed as 1/(1+pct/100)−1 and not just −pct.
(4) If the owner wants sentiment colouring for FX, make it an explicit per-instrument flag (for example `invertColor: true` on usdmxn, eurmxn and dxy) that the same helper reads. Then every widget changes together and the choice is documented. Do not describe a weaker peso as a clear loss, because users with USD holdings gain in MXN terms.

findings.title: DataRow and the Indicadores grid remove the minus sign, so direction is shown by colour alone
findings.evidence: {up ? "+" : ""}{Math.abs(pct).toFixed(2)}% (3775) and {up ? "+" : ""}{Math.abs(d.pct).toFixed(2)}% (3917).
findings.why: A −1.30% move renders as '1.30%' in red. Colour-blind users (about 8% of men) and anyone reading a screenshot, print-out or copied text cannot tell losses from gains. This violates WCAG 1.4.1 (Use of Color). It also clashes with the bento grid and GlobalMarketsTable, which do show the sign.
findings.fix: Render the signed value, e.g. `${pct >= 0 ? "+" : "−"}${Math.abs(pct).toFixed(2)}%` using the typographic minus, and add ▲/▼ as MktCard does. Put this in a shared fmtPct helper.
findings.verify_reasoning:
I checked the code and the finding holds. The severity (medium) and the fix direction are right.

1. DataRow is defined at src/App.jsx:3749-3779. It sets `up = !isN && pct >= 0` and `cc = up ? "var(--positive)" : "var(--negative)"`, then renders `{up ? "+" : ""}{Math.abs(pct).toFixed(2)}%` at line 3775. A negative pct therefore shows as an unsigned number in red. The hero variant (the IPC row, line 4051) goes further and signals direction with a tinted background (`bg` = positive-soft or negative-soft) and a coloured left border, which is still colour only.
2. DataRow is used for the IPC hero row, USD/MXN, EUR/MXN, EUR/USD, GBP/USD and USD/JPY (4051-4063), the eight commodity and crypto rows (4113) and the five global indices (4129). So every daily move in these panels loses its sign when it is negative.
3. The Indicadores Principales grid (3887-3921) does the same at line 3917: `{up ? "+" : ""}{Math.abs(d.pct).toFixed(2)}%`. This covers S&P 500, NASDAQ, Dow, IPC, VIX, DXY, US 10Y and USD/MXN.
4. The inconsistency claim is also correct:
   - The bento grid (3869) prints `{up ? "+" : ""}{d.change_pct.toFixed(2)}%` with no Math.abs, so the minus sign appears.
   - GlobalMarketsTable (563) prints `${up ? "+" : ""}${p.toFixed(2)}%`, so the sign appears.
   - MktCard (599) also uses Math.abs, but line 624 adds `{up ? "▲" : "▼"}`, so direction is still shown without relying on colour.
5. Nothing else in the code makes up for it: there is no arrow, no aria-label and no text cue on these two components. There is also no shared fmtPct helper; the repo has none.
6. On the principle: WCAG 2.x SC 1.4.1 (Use of Color) says colour must not be the only way information is conveyed, and here gain versus loss is conveyed only by colour. Copied text, screenshots, monochrome prints and red-green colour-vision deficiency (about 8% of men) all lose the information. For a finance terminal, the sign of a move is exactly the kind of information users act on.

Details and nuances:
- The same pattern appears at 3033: `({Math.abs(pnlPct).toFixed(2)}%)`. There the dollar P&L just before it carries the sign (`pnl >= 0 ? "+" : "−"`), so it is only a minor inconsistency, not a violation.
- The typographic minus (U+2212) looks better in a monospace terminal, but Excel and Google Sheets do not read it as negative when text is copied and pasted. If users are likely to copy numbers into spreadsheets, the ASCII hyphen-minus is safer.
- The helper should round before choosing the sign. Otherwise a value like -0.001 displays as a red "−0.00%".

findings.title: The global markets table shows USD returns of US-listed ETFs, which include FX and trade out of sync with local markets, and the source is mislabelled
findings.evidence: COUNTRY_ROWS maps each country to an ETF (EWJ, FXI, INDA, EWY...). The footer reads 'Retorno diario · iShares ETFs · desc. por rendimiento', but SPY is SPDR, not iShares. When data is null and loading is false the table shows 'Cargando datos de mercados globales…' indefinitely.
findings.why: EWJ and EWY trade during New York hours, after Tokyo and Seoul have closed, so their daily return reflects US-session news plus the yen/won move against USD, not 'Japan's market today'. For a Mexican user the return is not in MXN either. A failed fetch looks like an endless load with no retry.
findings.fix: Label the table 'Retorno diario en USD de ETFs de país listados en EE.UU. (incluye tipo de cambio, horario NY)', or for the major markets show the local indices already in _MARKET_SYMS (^N225, ^GDAXI, ^FTSE, ^HSI, ^MXX) with their local close date. Correct the footer to 'ETFs iShares / SPDR'. Add an error state with a Reintentar button.
findings.verify_reasoning:
Checked against the code. The main claims hold.

1. Mislabelled source. src/App.jsx:4035 renders the footer "Retorno diario · iShares ETFs · desc. por rendimiento". COUNTRY_ROWS (App.jsx:494-521) and backend _WORLDMAP_SYMS (backend.py:707-715) include SPY, which is a State Street SPDR fund. The other 25 tickers are iShares (EWG, EWJ, FXI, INDA, KSA, TUR, EPOL and the rest).

2. Returns are USD returns during NY hours. backend.py:717-725 sends _WORLDMAP_SYMS through _bulk_download (backend.py:644-693). change_pct is the percent change between the last two daily closes of the US-listed ETF (auto_adjust=True, so it is effectively a total return). For EWJ, EWY, EWT, FXI, INDA and the other Asian and European funds, the underlying market had already closed when the ETF traded. So the number mixes the local move, the USD/local-currency move, and news from the US session: r_ETF ≈ r_local + r_FX + premium/discount drift. It is not "Japan today". The row labels (App.jsx:555) show only the country name, and the footer never says USD. The table sits on the same tab as the IPC panel (App.jsx:4043+), which shows ^MXX in MXN. On a day when USDMXN moves, EWW and IPC can show opposite signs, which is a concrete source of confusion.

3. Endless "Cargando…". Confirmed only for network or JSON-parse failures. loadWorldMap (App.jsx:1956-1963) swallows the error, leaves data null and sets loading to false, so App.jsx:530-532 shows "Cargando datos de mercados globales…" with no retry button.

Where the finding is incomplete or partly wrong:

(a) It misses the more likely failure. When yfinance is rate-limited, _bulk_download returns {}. The router (backend.py:1920-1926) always answers HTTP 200, with {} or {"error": ...}, and the frontend never checks r.ok, data.error or empty data. Because {} is truthy, the user gets 26 rows of "—" and no message. That broken state is at least as common as the endless load. The backend caches the empty result for 60 s (backend.py:69-92, ok=bool).

(b) "No retry" is not quite true. The effect at App.jsx:1965-1971 calls loadWorldMap again if worldMapData is null when the user returns to the "news" tab. There is no explicit retry, though.

(c) Missed issue: once loaded, the data never refreshes. The 60 s interval at App.jsx:1973-1978 refreshes only loadMarketData, and the tab effect loads the world map only when worldMapData is null. The panel therefore shows a return that can be hours old, and there is no as-of date anywhere; the backend does not return the bar date. Before the US open it silently shows the previous session.

(d) The alternative fix is flawed. Swapping local indices (^N225, ^GDAXI, ^FTSE, ^HSI, ^MXX) into a list ranked by return mixes local-currency and USD returns. The sort at App.jsx:534-536 would then compare JPY returns with USD returns, which is a worse error. A cross-country ranking needs a common currency, so USD-denominated ETF returns are a defensible basis. The real problem is the labelling. Local indices belong in a separate block, not in this ranked list.

Medium severity is fair. Nobody acts on these numbers the way they would on a valuation, but the panel is misleading as labelled.
findings.corrected_fix:
1. Labelling (App.jsx:4034-4036): change the footer to "Retorno diario en USD · ETFs de país listados en EE.UU. (iShares; EE.UU. = SPY, SPDR) · horario NY, incluye tipo de cambio · orden: mayor a menor". Add a tooltip or info icon explaining that for Asia and Europe the move includes currency and news from after the local close.

2. As-of date: in _bulk_download (backend.py:660-666 and 677-683), add "date": str(col.index[-1].date()) (hist.index[-1] in the fallback path). Show "Cierre/último: {date}" in the footer, and mark "intradía" when the date is today and the time is before the 15:00 CDMX close.

3. MXN view for Mexican users: marketData.usdmxn.change_pct is already loaded on the same tab (md, App.jsx:3722). Add a USD/MXN toggle that computes r_MXN = (1 + r_USD/100) × (1 + r_USDMXN/100) − 1, then re-sorts. Keep the whole list in one currency; never mix local indices into this ranked list. If local indices are wanted, put them in a separate "Índices locales (moneda local, cierre local)" block built from _MARKET_SYMS, with each index's close date.

4. Error handling (App.jsx:1956-1963 and 525-532): add a worldMapError state. In loadWorldMap, check `if (!r.ok) throw`, then treat `data?.error` or `Object.keys(data).length === 0` (or zero rows with change_pct) as a failure, and clear the error on success. In GlobalMarketsTable, show "No se pudieron cargar los mercados globales" with a "Reintentar" button that calls loadWorldMap. Show the endless-load text only while loading is true.

5. Freshness: include loadWorldMap in the auto-refresh interval at App.jsx:1973-1978, for example every 5 minutes to match the backend TTL of 300 s, or re-fetch whenever the tab is entered instead of only when worldMapData is null.

findings.title: The RSS parser labels every feed 'Yahoo Finance' and leaves HTML entities and markup undecoded
findings.evidence: return (m.group(1).strip().replace("<![CDATA[","").replace("]]>","") ...); desc = _tag("description")[:250]; items.append({... "publisher": "Yahoo Finance", ...}). This runs for MarketWatch, CNBC, Seeking Alpha and Investing.com feeds as well.
findings.why:
Wrong attribution is a credibility and journalism-ethics problem: a CNBC or MarketWatch story shown as Yahoo Finance. RSS titles without CDATA use XML escaping, so 'S&P 500' and ''' show up literally in React. Descriptions containing

/ render as raw tags, and cutting at 250 characters can split an entity or tag. Regex parsing also misses RSS 1.0 () and Atom ().
findings.fix: Parse with xml.etree.ElementTree (or feedparser). Apply html.unescape() and strip tags (re.sub(r'<[^>]+>','',s)) before truncating. Pass the publisher per feed, e.g. a list of (url, 'MarketWatch') tuples, or read <channel><title>.
findings.verify_reasoning:
I read backend.py lines 728-803 and the frontend code that renders this data. The core claims hold. A few side details are overstated, but none of them change the finding. 1) Wrong publisher, confirmed. backend.py:750 sets `"publisher": "Yahoo Finance"` for every item `_rss_news(url)` returns. The only caller is `get_market_news` (backend.py:793-800), which runs it over MarketWatch (feeds.content.dowjones.io), CNBC, Seeking Alpha and Investing.com as well as Yahoo (backend.py:777-792). The label is shown to users by `MarketNewsItem` at src/App.jsx:786 (`{item.publisher && ...{item.publisher}}`), which is used on the market news lists at App.jsx:4169 and 4226. The per-ticker news path (`_extract_news_item`, backend.py:1786-1799) reads the real provider and is not affected, so the bug only hits the market-news fallback. 2) Entities are not decoded, confirmed. `_tag` (backend.py:737-739) only removes the CDATA markers. There is no `html.unescape` anywhere in backend.py (grep finds no `import html`). The frontend has no `dangerouslySetInnerHTML` and no decoder either. React renders `{item.title}` and `{item.summary}` as plain text (App.jsx:783-784), so a non-CDATA title such as `S&P 500` or `'` appears literally. `desc[:250]` at line 742 slices the raw string, so it can cut an entity or tag in half. Any HTML inside a CDATA description (for example `

` or ``) would also appear as literal text, and it feeds `classify_sentiment` at line 799, which pollutes the sentiment result. Whether a given feed actually sends HTML varies by feed, so this part is likely rather than certain. 3) Overstated details. All nine configured feeds are RSS 2.0, so "misses RSS 1.0 / Atom" is hypothetical today. The related real weakness is that the pattern `(.*?)` (line 735) only matches a bare `` tag, so `` or any `` with attributes is silently skipped. Also, `_tag("link")`'s pattern `]*>` would also match other tags that start with `link`, and a self-closing tag like `` could make it match wrongly. 4) Severity and scope. This only runs when yfinance returns fewer than 5 items (line 776). The code's own comment notes yfinance news "puede fallar en cloud", so on Render this fallback is probably the normal path. Medium severity is right: it is a credibility and readability problem, not wrong financial numbers. 5) Fix caveats. The suggested fix has two problems. First, `xml.etree.ElementTree` rejects the malformed XML that real-world feeds often contain, and parsing untrusted remote XML with it is not recommended (use defusedxml instead). Second, `feedparser` is not in requirements.txt (only yfinance and requests), so using it means adding a dependency. The fix below corrects both. The finding's order of `html.unescape` and tag stripping also needs refining: some feeds escape their HTML (`<p>`), so you need to unescape, strip tags, then unescape again.
findings.corrected_fix: In backend.py: (a) Pass the source name into the parser instead of hardcoding it. Change `rss_feeds` (lines 777-792) to a list of tuples, e.g. `("https://feeds.finance.yahoo.com/rss/2.0/headline?s=%5EGSPC®ion=US&lang=en-US", "Yahoo Finance")`, `("https://feeds.content.dowjones.io/public/rss/mw_topstories", "MarketWatch")`, `("https://www.cnbc.com/id/100003114/device/rss/rss.html", "CNBC")`, `("https://seekingalpha.com/market_currents.xml", "Seeking Alpha")`, `("https://www.investing.com/rss/news.rss", "Investing.com")`. Change the signature to `def _rss_news(url: str, publisher: str) -> list:` and call it as `for feed, pub in rss_feeds: ... _rss_news(feed, pub)`. At line 750 use `"publisher": publisher`. If you prefer to read ``, keep the per-feed name as the fallback anyway, because channel titles are often long, like "MarketWatch.com - Top Stories". (b) Clean the text before truncating it. Add `import html` at the top and a helper: ```python def _clean(s: str, limit: int | None = None) -> str: s = s.replace("<![CDATA[", "").replace("]]>", "") s = html.unescape(s) # <p> -> <p>, & -> & s = re.sub(r"<[^>]+>", " ", s) # strip tags s = html.unescape(s) # entities that were inside the HTML s = re.sub(r"\s+", " ", s).strip() if limit and len(s) > limit: s = s[:limit].rsplit(" ", 1)[0] + "…" return s ``` Have `_tag` return the raw inner text, then set `title = _clean(_tag("title"))` and `desc = _clean(_tag("description"), 250)`. Unescape the link as well (`html.unescape(link)`), because `&` inside URLs otherwise breaks the query strings. Since classify_sentiment runs on title plus summary, it will then score clean text. (c) Make the patterns tolerant of attributes: use `re.findall(r"<item\b[^>]*>(.*?)</item>", text, re.S)` for items (and optionally `<entry\b[^>]*>` for Atom). In `_tag`, use `rf"<{tag}\b[^>]*>(.*?)</{tag}>"` so `<link` cannot match other tags that start with `link`. As an alternative to (b) and (c), add `feedparser` to requirements.txt and use `feedparser.parse(resp.content)`. It handles RSS 0.9x/1.0/2.0 and Atom, entities and malformed feeds, and exposes `entry.title`, `entry.summary`, `entry.link` and `entry.published_parsed`. You would still apply tag stripping and truncation to `summary`. Do not use plain `xml.etree.ElementTree` on remote feeds: it fails on malformed XML and is not safe for untrusted input (use defusedxml if you choose stdlib XML).

findings.title: Market news is not cached; each click triggers up to 15 sequential upstream requests
findings.evidence: elif parts[0] == "news" and len(parts) > 1 and parts[1] == "market": result = get_market_news(). get_market_news loops over 6 tickers calling yft(ticker).news, then over up to 9 feeds with _session.get(url, timeout=6), all sequentially. Every other market endpoint is wrapped in _cached().
findings.why: Worst case is roughly 6 Yahoo calls plus 9×6 s of RSS timeouts, close to a minute per request on Render's free tier. Every user hitting '↻ Noticias' repeats this, which invites Yahoo rate-limiting. That in turn breaks /market and /macro, which share the same Yahoo quota.
findings.fix: Wrap it: return _cached("market_news", _get_market_news_fresh, ttl=300, ok=lambda r: len(r.get("news", []))>0). Fetch tickers and feeds in parallel with ThreadPoolExecutor and a total time budget.
findings.verify_reasoning:
The main point is correct. Some supporting claims are wrong or overstated.

What the code confirms:
- backend.py:1891 routes /news/market straight to get_market_news() with no cache layer.
- get_market_news (756-803) calls yft(ticker).news one at a time for 6 tickers (761-773).
- If that returns fewer than 5 items (776), it fetches up to 9 RSS feeds one at a time through _rss_news, which uses _session.get(url, timeout=6) (732). The loop stops early once it has 20 items (794).
- So the worst case really is 15 sequential upstream calls. The 6 s is a per-phase connect/read timeout, not a total cap, so "close to a minute" is a realistic worst case.
- The worst case happens exactly when Yahoo is failing or throttling, which is when a cache helps most.
- The frontend (App.jsx:1946-1953) calls this on the first visit to the news tab (1968) and on every click of "↻ Noticias" (3823). The fetch has no AbortSignal timeout, unlike /stock and /fx.

What is wrong or overstated:
1. "Every other market endpoint is wrapped in _cached()" is false. _cached is used only by macro (626), market (704), worldmap (725), edgar (1175), magic (1337) and fx_hist inside chart (498); rf caches by hand (1820-1835). get_fx (441), get_fibras (1466), get_news(ticker) (1801), get_stock, get_insiders, get_momentum, get_returns and get_dcf have no cache. get_fibras is market-wide and loops over the whole FIBRA list with several Yahoo calls per ticker, so it is a worse offender than news. This endpoint is one of several uncached ones, not the only one.
2. The server is a ThreadingHTTPServer (line 10), so a slow news request does not block other requests. The auto-refresh timer (App.jsx:1975) only calls loadMarketData, not news. Load therefore comes from explicit user actions and first tab visits, not polling.
3. "Rate-limiting here breaks /market and /macro" is speculative. The code shares a yfinance session, but about 6 news calls per page view is modest next to the bulk downloads. /market and /macro are cached 120 s and 300 s, so they absorb short throttling.
4. On the fix: a total time budget does not work with `with ThreadPoolExecutor(...)`, because leaving that block waits for every thread (up to the 6 s timeouts). You need concurrent.futures.wait(..., timeout=...) followed by shutdown(wait=False, cancel_futures=True). Merge results in the original ticker/feed order so dedup priority stays the same. Running yfinance in parallel is already done elsewhere (lines 577, 690, 1298), so thread safety is not a new risk.

Related bug seen while checking (separate issue): _rss_news hardcodes publisher "Yahoo Finance" (750) for CNBC, MarketWatch, Seeking Alpha and Investing.com items, so the source shown to users is wrong.

Medium severity is fair, arguably low-medium. This is a reliability and latency problem, not wrong numbers.

findings.title: Macro and world-map data are fetched once and never refreshed, while market quotes refresh every 60 s
findings.evidence: fetch(`${BACKEND}/macro`).then(r => r.json()).then(setMacroData).catch(() => {}); runs in a mount-only effect. The interval is setInterval(loadMarketData, 60_000), which covers /market only. The '↻ Mercados' button calls loadMarketData() only. loadWorldMap runs once when the tab opens if there is no data yet.
findings.why: In a long session the gauge, the Resumen VIX/10Y/spread lines and the header strip freeze at page-load values, while the bento tiles next to them update. A failed /macro call is swallowed silently, so those widgets disappear with no explanation.
findings.fix: Create a loadMacro callback. Refresh macro and worldmap on the same interval as their server TTL (300 s) and from the '↻ Mercados' button. Show an error or retry state when macroData is missing.
findings.verify_reasoning:
The mechanics check out. I read every cited line.
- Line 1236 fetches /macro once, inside the mount-only effect at lines 1232-1238. Its error handler is `.catch(() => {})`.
- The only timer is `setInterval(loadMarketData, 60_000)` at line 1976, and it runs only while the news tab is open.
- The '↻ Mercados' button (lines 3815-3822) calls only `loadMarketData()`.
- Nothing ever re-fetches `macroData`. It feeds the global header strip (lines 2237-2255), the Fear & Greed gauge (`vixVal` at 3745, drawn at 3986-4027) and the VIX and 10Y lines in ResumenManero (658-668).

So the core claim stands. The details need correcting:

1. **Polling /macro will not make these widgets live.** The main sources in `_get_macro_fresh` (backend.py 569-622) are all end-of-day data:
   - `_fred_rate('DGS10'/'DGS2')` reads FRED's daily CSV, which lags about one business day (lines 516-531).
   - `_cboe_vix` reads CBOE's `VIX_History.csv` of daily closes (534-547).
   - `_stooq_dxy` reads Stooq daily bars (`i=d`, 550-561).
   
   A 300 s poll would return the same numbers all day. It only helps when the date rolls over, or to retry after a failure. The real user-visible problem is that the same screen shows two different numbers:
   - 'Indicadores Principales' lists vix, dxy and t10y without `macro: true` (lines 3892-3894). So `C()` at 3724-3726 reads them from `md`, i.e. /market. That is Yahoo's intraday ^VIX, DX-Y.NYB and ^TNX, refreshed every 60 s.
   - The gauge, the Resumen and the header strip, on the same page, show CBOE's previous-close VIX and FRED's 10Y.
   
   A user can therefore see two different VIX values at once.
2. **Related bug: a fake '+0.00' change.** The backend hard-codes `"change": 0` for the FRED, CBOE and Stooq values (backend.py 575, 587, 589). The header strip renders `m.chg != null` (line 2248), so VIX, DXY and 10Y always show a green '+0.00'.
3. **World map: 'runs once' is a bit overstated.** Line 1969 retries each time you re-enter the tab if `worldMapData` is still null. But:
   - An empty `{}` response or an error body is truthy, so it is never retried.
   - It is never refreshed while the tab stays open, and yfinance's daily bars include today's partial bar, so these ETF returns do move during the day.
   
   The 300 s server TTL is confirmed (backend.py 725).
4. **Silent failure: mostly correct.** Workspace only mounts after /health succeeds (lines 1002-1015, `detectBackend` with a 60 s timeout), so Render cold starts are largely covered. But if every source fails, `_cached(..., ok=bool)` still returns `{}` (backend.py 626, `fail_ttl` 60). Then `macroData = {}`: the header strip renders an empty container, the gauge disappears, nothing is shown and nothing is retried.
5. **Minor:** /market's TTL is 120 s (backend.py 704), so every other 60 s poll returns the same cached data.

Medium severity is fair, driven mainly by the conflicting VIX/10Y numbers and the fake '+0.00' change rather than by missed updates.

findings.title: The Resumen draws causal and advice-like conclusions from single-day moves
findings.evidence: 'Oro avanza ... — demanda de refugio activa' / 'menor apetito por safe-haven'; 'WTI ... — presión inflacionaria en energía'; 'VIX ... volatilidad elevada, cautela recomendada'; 'ambiente de calma, risk-on'; '10Y' coloured negative only when r > 5.
findings.why: A one-day gold move is driven as much by real yields and the dollar as by safe-haven demand, so asserting the cause is not supported. A one-day oil move says little about inflation. 'Cautela recomendada' is investment guidance. The 5% cutoff for the 10Y is arbitrary. The summary also leaves out the drivers that matter most for this audience: peso vs DXY, Banxico, CETES and the US-MX rate spread.
findings.fix: Rephrase as descriptive plus conditional text, e.g. 'Oro +0.8% (suele subir con dólar débil o menor tasa real)'. Remove the imperative advice. Base thresholds on percentiles or changes (e.g. VIX above its 1y 80th percentile, 10Y change in bp). Add lines for DXY vs peso and the Banxico/CETES spread once that data exists.
findings.verify_reasoning:
The cited code is accurate. In src/App.jsx:
- L673 prints "demanda de refugio activa" / "menor apetito por safe-haven" just from the sign of md.gold.change_pct.
- L678 prints "presión inflacionaria en energía" / "alivio en precios de energía" from the sign of the WTI change.
- L662 maps VIX >30 to "risk-off", 20-30 to "volatilidad elevada, cautela recomendada" and <=20 to "ambiente de calma, risk-on".
- L667 sets the 10Y colour to `r > 5 ? negative : warning`, so it is never green.

The core point holds. A one-day gold move is driven by real yields and the dollar as much as by safe-haven flows. One day of WTI says almost nothing about inflation. "Cautela recomendada" is advice-like wording in an app with no disclaimer (grep finds no "asesoría" or "no constituye" anywhere). The 5% line for the 10Y level is arbitrary.

Some details need correcting:
1) VIX is a level, not a one-day move. 20 and 30 are standard rules of thumb (the long-run mean is about 19-20; 30 is the usual stress line), so they are defensible. Only the "cautela recomendada" and "risk-on" wording is the problem. A 1y percentile is optional, not required.
2) The finding misses a bigger issue in the same block. L687 counts every `var(--warning)` insight as POSITIVE for the "Sentimiento" pill (L689). So:
   - the 10Y always votes positive;
   - VIX 20-30 ("volatilidad elevada") votes positive;
   - gold up ("refugio", a risk-off reading) votes positive;
   - WTI up ("presión inflacionaria") votes positive.
   WTI down is coloured red and counted negative even though its own text says "alivio". The colour, the text and the mood tally contradict each other, and the headline sentiment is biased upward.
3) "Add DXY once that data exists" is partly wrong. macroData.dxy already exists (backend.py L588-589 via Stooq, shown at App.jsx L2242 and L4068), but its change is hard-coded to 0. The FRED 10Y and 2Y entries also always have change 0 (backend.py L575, and _fred_rate L516-531 returns only the last observation). A "10Y change in bp" fix therefore needs backend work first.
4) The peso is already covered (L653-657). Banxico and TIIE exist only as hard-coded, stale MX_REF values (L3732-3733, "Banxico May 2026"). CETES and the MX-US spread have no live data.

Severity medium is appropriate. The mood-tally bug makes the headline pill actively misleading.
findings.corrected_fix:
src/App.jsx ResumenManero (L658-690):
(a) Gold L673: make the text descriptive, e.g. `Oro ${sign}${pct}% a $X/oz` plus a neutral hint such as "(sensible a tasas reales y al dólar)". Drop the causal "demanda de refugio" claim. If a causal read is wanted, show it only when gold is up AND DXY is flat or up AND VIX is rising.
(b) WTI L678: descriptive only, e.g. "WTI +1.2% a $X/bbl". Remove "presión inflacionaria". If kept, only mention energy-inflation pressure on multi-week moves (for example a 1-month change above 10%).
(c) VIX L662: keep the 20/30 bands, but label them "calma (<20)", "elevada (20-30)" and "estrés (>30)". Remove "cautela recomendada" and "risk-on/risk-off". Optionally add the 1y percentile.
(d) 10Y L667: colour and text by change, not level. In backend.py, change _fred_rate to return the last two valid observations and set change = (v_t - v_{t-1}) * 100 bp (also for DGS2, so the spread change works too). Then display "10Y 4.12% (+6 pb)" with neutral colouring. Keep the inverted-curve flag.
(e) Fix the mood tally (L687-689): give each insight an explicit `tone: +1 | 0 | -1` for risk sentiment and stop inferring it from colour. Equities up = +1. USDMXN up = -1. VIX >30 = -1, VIX <20 = +1. Gold, WTI and 10Y = 0 (ambiguous). Rename the pill to "Tono de mercado (indicativo)".
(f) Mexico-relevant lines:
   - DXY: in backend.py _stooq_dxy, compute the change from the previous CSV row (it already downloads the daily history) instead of `change: 0`. Then add "Peso vs DXY" (whether MXN moves are idiosyncratic or broad-dollar).
   - Banxico/CETES: fetch live data (Banxico SIE API series SF43783 for the 28d CETES and SF61745 for the target rate) instead of the hard-coded MX_REF. Then add the "CETES 28d − T-bill 3m" carry spread.
(g) Add a one-line footer: "Información descriptiva, no constituye recomendación de inversión." Also note that VIX (CBOE CSV) and the 10Y (FRED) are prior-close values despite the "LIVE" badge at L708.

findings.title: News dedup is exact-URL only, and there are no Spanish or Mexican sources for a Spanish UI aimed at MX investors
findings.evidence: if not parsed["title"] or parsed["url"] in seen: continue ... if item["url"] not in seen. The only sources are yfinance news for ^MXX/^GSPC/USDMXN=X/GC=F/CL=F/BTC-USD plus English US feeds.
findings.why: The same wire story, reached through different URLs (tracking parameters, Yahoo vs original publisher), appears several times. Every headline is in English. There is no coverage of Banxico announcements, BMV issuers or Mexican fiscal news, even though those move the IPC, the peso and FIBRAs.
findings.fix: Normalize URLs (strip the query string and fragment) and add title dedup (lowercased alphanumeric tokens with Jaccard > 0.8). Add Mexican Spanish-language feeds (El Economista, El Financiero, Expansión, Banxico press releases). Tag each item with a region and add an 'MX / EE.UU. / Global' filter.

findings.title: The 10Y-2Y spread is shown in inconsistent units; the debug endpoint still labels ^IRX as 't2y'; 10Y-3M is missing
findings.evidence: Resumen: `Spread ${...}${Math.round(sp.value * 100)} pb`. Header: `${macroData.spread.value > 0 ? "+" : ""}${macroData.spread.value}` (raw, e.g. '+0.55', no unit). Gauge footer: macroData.spread.inverted ? "⚠ Inv." : `Spread +${macroData.spread.value.toFixed(2)}`. Debug: _bulk_download({... "^IRX":"t2y" ...}).
findings.why: The same spread appears as '+55 pb' and as '+0.55' with no unit, and when the curve is inverted the gauge footer hides the value entirely. The debug endpoint repeats the ^IRX = 2Y mislabel that the main path deliberately fixed. The NY Fed recession model uses the 10Y-3M spread (FRED T10Y3M), which is the better recession signal.
findings.fix: Always show the spread in basis points with a sign (e.g. '−35 pb (invertida)'). Rename the debug key to 't13w'. Add T10Y3M from FRED next to 10Y-2Y, with a tooltip noting that an inversion is historically a lagging-probability signal, not a timing tool.

findings.title: Style Box computes heat intensity and then discards it; the 'Core' column is the parent index and uses non-standard naming
findings.evidence: toCell() computes intensity and bg via color-mix, but the call site destructures `const { p, bg: _bg, fg: _fg } = toCell(k);` and uses flat cellBg = isUp ? "var(--positive-soft)" : ... Core cells are IVV, IJH and IJR, the full S&P 500/400/600. Only 1-day % is shown.
findings.why: Every green cell is the same shade, so +0.05% and +2.5% look identical and the heat-map loses its purpose. The full parent index is not a separate 'core' style bucket: S&P Value and Growth overlap and together make up the parent. Morningstar calls this column 'Blend'. A single day of style returns is mostly noise. Style rotation is read over 1W/1M/YTD, and relative to the blend.
findings.fix: Use the computed bg (intensity scaled to |p|). Rename the column 'Blend (índice)'. Add period toggles (1D/1S/1M/YTD) using closes already fetched. Optionally show Value−Growth and Small−Large spreads as factor readings.

findings.title: News cards keep 'hace X' frozen after a refresh (index keys plus mount-time clock) and cut headlines to one line
findings.evidence: const [nowSec] = useState(() => Math.floor(Date.now() / 1000)); items are rendered with key={i}. Title style: whiteSpace: "nowrap", textOverflow: "ellipsis". Neutral uses var(--warning).
findings.why: With index keys, a refreshed list reuses old components, so nowSec stays at the first mount and ages are understated. Future-dated items would render negative minutes. Single-line truncation reduces headlines to a few words on mobile. Amber for 'Neutral' reads as a warning.
findings.fix: Key by item.url. Compute now once per render in the parent, or refresh it on a 60 s tick, and clamp to 0. Use a 2-line clamp (display:-webkit-box; WebkitLineClamp:2). Colour neutral var(--muted).

findings.title: Dead or misleading code in the market area: unused MktCard, unused _make_entry, misplaced comment; LineChart has no tooltip and breaks on empty data
findings.evidence: '// ─── LOADING SPINNER' sits above function LineChart. MktCard is never referenced (grep shows only its definition), and its borderBottom accent is overridden by the later `border` shorthand. _make_entry has no callers. LineChart does Math.min(...allVals) with no guard for empty data, which yields Infinity and NaN paths.
findings.why: Dead code in a 5,500-line file slows maintenance. A Bloomberg-like return chart without a hover crosshair and values is much less useful. Empty series render a broken SVG instead of an empty state.
findings.fix: Delete MktCard and _make_entry, or wire them up and fix the border order. Move the comment. Have LineChart return an empty-state message when allVals.length === 0, and add a pointer-move crosshair showing the date and each series' value.

findings.title: Login password is hardcoded in the client bundle and the session is a localStorage flag; the backend /login is never used
findings.evidence: handleSubmit: `if (pw === "Investments") { onAuth(); }`. readAuthed: `localStorage.getItem(AUTH_KEY) === "1"`. Meanwhile backend.py:1855-1862 has check_login() with hmac.compare_digest and a POST /login route (backend.py:1950-1956) that the frontend never calls (grep '/login' in App.jsx finds nothing).
findings.why: Anyone can read the password from the shipped JS, or skip it with `localStorage.setItem('kaizen_authed','1')`. Data endpoints are not gated. For a product that companies would hand to employees there is no per-user identity, no revocation and no audit.
findings.fix: Add a username field. POST {username,password} to /login and have the backend issue a signed, expiring token (HttpOnly cookie or JWT). Require it on all data routes and store only the token client-side. Delete the literal "Investments" from the bundle. Show real error states: 401 means 'Usuario o contraseña incorrectos', 429 means too many attempts.
findings.verify_reasoning:
I checked every factual claim against the code and all of them hold.

1. **Password hardcoded in the client.** src/App.jsx:932-942 `handleSubmit` does `if (pw === "Investments") { onAuth(); }`. The literal also appears in the shipped bundle: grep finds "Investments" in dist/assets/index-BNl03Xe4.js.

2. **Session is just a localStorage flag.** App.jsx:52-60 defines `AUTH_KEY = "kaizen_authed"`. `readAuthed()` returns `localStorage.getItem(AUTH_KEY) === "1"`. App.jsx:1005 seeds `useState(readAuthed)`. App.jsx:1039 calls `writeAuthed(true)` on success. Running `localStorage.setItem('kaizen_authed','1')` and reloading skips the login. The VITE_SKIP_LOGIN bypass is correctly limited to DEV builds, so it is not an extra hole.

3. **Backend login exists but is never called.** backend.py:1844-1862 reads a `USERS` JSON env var and compares with `hmac.compare_digest`. backend.py:1950-1956 handles POST /login. The frontend has no call to /login. Every fetch in App.jsx (lines 40-1959) is unauthenticated.

4. **Data routes are not gated.** backend.py `do_GET` (1876-1922) serves every route with no auth check, including /debug/macro, which runs live FRED, CBOE, Stooq and Yahoo calls. `_cors()` (1969-1972) sends `Access-Control-Allow-Origin: *`.

Details the finding gets wrong or leaves out:

- **The login route cannot drive the error states the fix describes.** It always answers HTTP 200 with `{ok:false, error:"Credenciales incorrectas"}` and issues no token. There is no rate limiting anywhere. "401" and "429" only become possible after new backend work.
- **Passwords in USERS are stored in plaintext** in the env var. They should be hashed.
- **The HttpOnly-cookie option won't work as written.** The frontend is on Vercel and the backend on Render, which are different sites. The cookie would need `SameSite=None; Secure`, credentialed fetches, a specific allowed origin instead of `*`, and `Access-Control-Allow-Credentials: true`. Even then, Safari and third-party-cookie blocking can break it. A bearer token or a same-origin Vercel proxy is more reliable.
- **"JWT" implies a dependency the backend doesn't have.** requirements.txt lists only yfinance and requests, and the server is a plain stdlib `BaseHTTPRequestHandler`. An HMAC-signed token built with the stdlib is the lighter option.

Severity: critical is defensible under the rubric (authentication bypass, for a product meant to be sold per seat to companies). But the impact is about access control, not data leakage. Everything behind the gate is public market data, and portfolios, screener lists and FIBRA data live only in each browser's localStorage (App.jsx:801-814, 1105-1134), so bypassing the gate exposes no other user's data. The real harms are:
- anyone can use the app, or call the Render backend directly;
- this uses up the free Render instance and the upstream rate limits (Yahoo, FRED);
- there is no per-user identity, revocation or audit trail.
findings.corrected_fix:
Backend (backend.py):

1. **Store hashes, not plaintext.** Keep `USERS` as `{"user": "scrypt$<salt_hex>$<hash_hex>"}` and verify with `hashlib.scrypt` plus `hmac.compare_digest`. Add a small admin script to generate the hashes.

2. **Return real status codes from POST /login.**
   - On success: HTTP 200 with `{token, expiresAt, user}`.
   - On bad credentials: HTTP 401.
   - Add an in-memory attempt limiter keyed by IP (X-Forwarded-For on Render) and by username, for example 5 failures per 15 minutes. When it trips, return HTTP 429 with a Retry-After header.

3. **Issue a stdlib signed token.** Format: `base64url(json{sub, exp, ver}) + "." + base64url(hmac_sha256(SECRET_KEY, payload))`. Set `SECRET_KEY` as a Render env var. Use a 12h expiry. Add a per-user `ver` counter or a revocation set so access can be revoked.

4. **Gate every route.** In `do_GET`, require `Authorization: Bearer <token>` for all routes except /health and OPTIONS. Return 401 if the token is missing or expired. `send_response` must use the real status code instead of always 200.

5. **Lock down debugging and CORS.**
   - Remove /debug/macro, or put it behind an admin role.
   - Change `_cors()` to echo only an allow-listed origin (the Vercel domain via an env var), and add `Vary: Origin`.
   - Allow only the headers actually used: `Authorization` and `Content-Type`.

6. **Log** each login success or failure with the username. This is the minimal audit trail.

Frontend (src/App.jsx):

1. **Rewrite the login.** Add a username field to `LoginScreen`, POST `{username, password}` to `${BACKEND}/login`, and delete the literal "Investments".
2. **Show real error states.**
   - 401: "Usuario o contraseña incorrectos".
   - 429: "Demasiados intentos, espera N min".
   - Network error: "Sin conexión al servidor".
   - Disable the submit button while the request is in flight.
3. **Replace the flag with the token.** Store `{token, exp}` instead of `kaizen_authed = "1"`. Keep it in memory plus sessionStorage, or in localStorage only if "recordarme" is ticked.
4. **Use one fetch wrapper.** Route every `fetch(`${BACKEND}/...`)` call through a single `api()` helper that adds the `Authorization` header and, on any 401, clears the token and returns to `LoginScreen`.
5. **Validate on reload.** `readAuthed()` should check `exp` locally and treat an expired token as logged out.

If HttpOnly cookies are preferred over bearer tokens, first put the backend on the same site with a Vercel rewrite (`/api/*` to the Render URL), then set `HttpOnly; Secure; SameSite=Lax`. Do not rely on cross-site cookies combined with `Access-Control-Allow-Origin: *`; that combination does not work.

findings.title: Análisis shows fabricated quarterly financials: annual figures divided by 4 with invented growth multipliers
findings.evidence: `// Simulate 4 quarters by dividing annual by 4 with minor variation` → `return [base * 0.88, base * 0.96, base * 1.05, base * 1.11];` applied to revenue, net income, and also to totalAssets and totalDebt, labeled Q1–Q4. Table rows with no matching bar ('Total Activos', 'Margen %', 'D/E ratio') print the annual value under every quarter (5384: `: val ?? "—"`). The only disclosure, '* anual estimado por trimestres', is color #374151 on bg-deep (5364), about 1.9:1 contrast.
findings.why: Users see a steady 26% intra-year growth trend that does not exist. Balance-sheet items are point-in-time stocks, not flows, so dividing assets or debt by 4 is conceptually wrong. The bar chart (assets/4) and the table (full assets in each column) contradict each other in the same panel. The disclosure is effectively invisible. People will act on these numbers.
findings.fix: Return real data from the backend: yfinance quarterly_income_stmt, quarterly_balance_sheet and quarterly_cashflow, or the 10-Q frames from the SEC EDGAR integration already in place. If quarterly data is missing, render one 'Anual (TTM)' column. Never synthesize values. Use Spanish labels with currency and units, e.g. 'Ingresos (mil M USD)'.
findings.verify_reasoning:
I read the code and every factual claim in the finding holds.

1) Fabrication (src/App.jsx:5019-5024). `quarters(annual)` returns `[base*0.88, base*0.96, base*1.05, base*1.11]` with `base = annual/4`. It is applied to revenue, net income, totalAssets, totalDebt, OCF and FCF (5028-5051), and the results are plotted under `QLABELS = ["Q1".."Q4"]` (5060, 5080-5084). 1.11/0.88 = 1.26, so the chart shows a made-up 26% rise from Q1 to Q4. The multipliers sum to 4.00, which keeps the yearly total the same but invents the trend. For a loss-making company it would show the loss getting steadily worse, which is also invented. Dividing assets and debt by 4 is wrong in concept: they are balances measured at a single date, not flows that accumulate over a period.

2) The inputs are not even one consistent period. In backend.py:219-268, `totalRevenue`, `netIncomeToCommon`, OCF and FCF come first from yfinance `.info`, which is trailing twelve months (TTM). `totalAssets`, and sometimes the other fields, fall back to `balance_sheet.iloc[0]` or `income_stmt.iloc[0]`, which is the latest fiscal year. Total debt can even fall back to 'Long Term Debt' only. So TTM figures and fiscal-year figures are mixed together, then split into fake quarters.

3) The table contradicts the chart (5375-5386). Each table row finds its chart series by checking whether the series name contains the first word of the row label (5376). The results:
- **Rows with fake quarterly values:** 'Revenue' matches 'Revenue', 'Net Income' matches via 'net', and 'Free Cash Flow' matches 'Free CF' via 'free'.
- **Rows repeating the full annual figure in all four quarter columns** (`: val ?? "—"`): 'Total Activos' ('total' is in neither 'Activos' nor 'Deuda'), 'Total Deuda', 'Oper. Cash Flow' ('oper.' is not in 'op. cf'), 'Margen %' and 'D/E ratio'.
So on the Balance tab the bars show roughly assets/4 while the table shows full assets under every quarter. The Cash Flow tab mixes the two behaviours in one table. The finding is right; it actually understates the problem, since the cash-flow rows are also inconsistent with each other.

4) The disclosure is effectively invisible (5364). The note is `color: "#374151"`, fontSize 10, inside `.dark-panel`, where theme.css:371 sets `--bg-deep: #07100b`. I computed the contrast at about 1.87:1, far below WCAG AA's 4.5:1 for normal text. Its wording ('anual estimado por trimestres') also doesn't say the growth pattern is made up.

5) Nothing else handles this. The SEC EDGAR panel right below (5394+) shows official figures, but only for US issuers and only annual. The fake panel still renders for every ticker, including .MX.

Severity 'critical' is justified: the app presents synthesized numbers labelled as quarterly results, and users could act on them.

Two corrections to the proposed fix, neither of which changes the verdict:
(a) 'the 10-Q frames from the SEC EDGAR integration already in place' overstates what exists. `get_edgar_financials` (backend.py:1144-1145) keeps only `form == "10-K"`, `fp == "FY"` facts lasting about a year (`_is_annual`, 350-380 days). No quarterly data is extracted yet, so it would have to be extended. Also, 10-Q cash-flow and income facts are often year-to-date (6 or 9 months), and there is no Q4 10-Q.
(b) EDGAR does not cover .MX tickers (backend.py:1091), so for Mexican users yfinance statements are the only source.

Side issue in the same panel: the 'D/E ratio' row shows yfinance `debtToEquity`, which is in percent (150 means 1.5x). The metrics thresholds at 5008 (`v < 50`, `v > 200`) confirm the percent scale, so labelling it a ratio or 'x' is misleading.
findings.corrected_fix:
Backend (backend.py get_stock, around lines 218-270 and the return dict around 415-431):
- Add a `statements` object built from yfinance `t.quarterly_income_stmt`, `t.quarterly_balance_sheet` and `t.quarterly_cashflow`. Take the last 4-5 columns and include each column's period-end date.
- Rows to include: Total Revenue, Net Income, Total Assets, Total Debt, Stockholders Equity, Operating Cash Flow, Free Cash Flow.
- If quarterly frames are empty (common for .MX tickers), fall back to the annual `t.income_stmt`, `t.balance_sheet` and `t.cashflow`. The code already fetches these as inc/bal/cf and currently uses only `.iloc[0]`. Label those columns as fiscal years.
- Return `financialCurrency` from `.info`, plus a `basis` flag ('quarterly' or 'annual') for each series.
- Optional, US tickers only: extend `get_edgar_financials` to also read `form == "10-Q"` facts. For flow concepts, keep only durations of about 80-100 days (drop the 6- and 9-month year-to-date facts). Derive Q4 as FY minus 9M YTD. For balance concepts, use the point-in-time value.

Frontend (src/App.jsx 5011-5060 and 5364-5391):
- Delete `quarters()` and the hard-coded `QLABELS`. Build column headers from the real period-end dates, e.g. '2T 2026 (jun)' or 'FY2025'.
- Plot balance-sheet items as levels. Never divide them.
- Replace the first-word substring matching at 5376 with an explicit key for each table row, e.g. `{ key: 'totalAssets', label: 'Activos totales' }`, so every row maps to its own series.
- Show '—' for a missing period. Never repeat the annual value across period columns.
- If no periodic data exists, show a single column labelled 'Últimos 12 meses (TTM)' for flow items or 'Último cierre (fecha)' for balance items, and don't draw a trend chart.
- Show ratios (margin, D/E) as their own rows computed per period from the real series, not one repeated value. Show D/E as `debtToEquity/100` with an 'x' suffix, or keep it as %.
- Replace the '* anual estimado por trimestres' note with a source and units line: 'Fuente: Yahoo Finance · cifras en miles de millones de {financialCurrency}'. Use `var(--muted-2)` (about 4.8:1 in .dark-panel), not #374151.
- Use Spanish row labels with units, e.g. 'Ingresos (miles de M MXN)'.
- For US tickers, consider merging this panel with the existing SEC EDGAR panel instead of keeping two financials panels.

findings.title: Mexico macro panel shows hardcoded, months-old INPC/TIIE/GDP values next to live data
findings.evidence: `const MX_REF = [ { label: "Inflación INPC", value: "4.53%", period: "1a Q Abr 2026" }, { label: "TIIE 28D", value: "7.02%", period: "Banxico May 2026" }, ... { label: "Reservas Intl.", value: "$256.5B" } ]`. These are rendered in the 'México · Macro' panel with the period in fontSize 8.
findings.why: As of Sep 2026 these values are 4-5 months stale. TIIE and INPC are the core inputs for a Mexican investor: real rates, CETES vs equities, FIBRA spreads. Placing them beside live quotes implies they are current, and the date is nearly unreadable.
findings.fix: Fetch from the Banxico SIE API (TIIE 28 SF43783, TIIE de fondeo SF60648, CETES 28 SF43936, objetivo SF61745) and the INEGI API (INPC) on the backend with caching. Show 'al <fecha>' at 11px or larger and a warning badge when older than one release cycle. Add CETES 28/91/364 and the Bono M 10A to this panel and to the top strip.
findings.verify_reasoning:
I checked the finding against the code and it holds.

1. The data is hardcoded. In /Users/luisalfredolizarragasanchez/Desktop/CLAUDE/05 NEWKAIZEN/src/App.jsx lines 3729-3737, `MX_REF` is a literal array built inside the `tab === "news"` IIFE. It holds INPC 4.53% ("1a Q Abr 2026"), PIB +0.2% ("Trim. INEGI"), TIIE Fondeo 1D 6.76% and TIIE 28D 7.02% (both "Banxico May 2026"), Desempleo 2.4% (Mar 2026), Deuda/PIB 50.4% (Q1 2026) and Reservas $256.5B (24 Abr 2026).
   - Nothing fetches or overrides these values. The backend has no Banxico/INEGI integration (grep for banxico/inegi/SIE/TIIE/CETES in backend.py finds nothing).
   - The only Mexican rate the backend fetches is `get_rf()` at backend.py:1814-1841. It pulls Bono M 10Y from FRED's monthly OECD series IRLTLT01MXM156N, which already lags by 1-2 months.

2. The rendering matches the finding. Lines 4072-4093 render each row in the "México · Macro" panel with the label at fontSize 9 and `r.period` at fontSize 8 in var(--muted) (line 4081). The value sits in a bold mono 13px pill with a colored background.
   - The Panel component (3783-3798) takes only a title, so there is no subtitle, footer, "referencia" tag or as-of badge.
   - The panel sits in the same `resp-grid-2` row as "México · Mercado" (4040-4069), which shows live IPC, USD/MXN and the US 10Y from marketData/macroData. Static and live values share the same row styling with no visual difference. A reader will assume the whole row is equally current.

3. The staleness is real. Today is 2026-09-22 and the period labels run from Mar to May 2026, so the data is 4-6 months old. Banxico has held several policy meetings since May, so the TIIE fondeo and TIIE 28 figures probably no longer match the current target. INPC is published every two weeks, so about ten releases have been missed.
   - For a Mexican investor, these are the numbers behind real-rate, CETES-vs-equity and FIBRA-spread decisions. That makes "high" severity defensible. It is not "critical" because a period label is shown, even if it is barely readable.

4. The app's own convention confirms the problem. Elsewhere the code avoids passing off fixed values as live: backend.py:1840-1841 labels its fallback "Bono M 10Y (ref. fija may 2026)" with `fallback: True`, and App.jsx:156-158 returns `ok:false`. The MX_REF panel has no such flag.

Refinements to the proposed fix (the core point is unaffected):
- Banxico SIE and INEGI both require a free API token. This needs env vars on Render; the finding does not mention it.
- SF43783 (TIIE 28), SF61745 (tasa objetivo) and SF43936 (CETES 28) are standard SIE series. SF60648 as "TIIE de fondeo" is doubtful: I believe the fondeo series is SF331451, but check the SIE catalog before coding it.
- Since January 2025, TIIE 28 can no longer be used as the reference rate in new contracts; Banxico now points to TIIE de fondeo. The headline rows should therefore be tasa objetivo and TIIE de fondeo, with TIIE 28 kept only as a legacy row.
- "PIB Q1 2026 +0.2%" does not say whether it is quarter-on-quarter seasonally adjusted or year-on-year. Label the basis.
findings.corrected_fix:
Backend (backend.py):
- Add `get_mx_macro()` and a `/mx-macro` route, reusing the existing `_cache_get`/`_cache_put` with a TTL of about 6 hours.
- Call Banxico SIE `https://www.banxico.org.mx/SieAPIRest/service/v1/series/{ids}/datos/oportuno` with header `Bmx-Token: os.environ["BANXICO_TOKEN"]`. Series (check each against the SIE catalog):
  - SF61745 tasa objetivo
  - TIIE de fondeo (believed to be SF331451, not SF60648)
  - SF43783 TIIE 28 (legacy row only)
  - SF43936 / SF43939 / SF43945 CETES 28 / 91 / 364 (latest weekly auction yield)
  - the SIE Bono M 10Y yield series, which is fresher than the FRED/OECD monthly data now used in get_rf; point get_rf at it too
  - SF43707 international reserves
  - annual INPC inflation (also available in SIE, so one token covers it; INEGI BIE with `INEGI_TOKEN` is the alternative, and also covers GDP and ENOE unemployment)
- Return per series: `{value, asOf, source, fallback:false}`.
- On failure, return the current literals with `fallback:true` and a label such as "ref. fija may 2026", following the existing get_rf convention at backend.py:1840-1841.

Frontend (App.jsx 3729-3737, 4072-4093):
- Replace the `MX_REF` literals with the fetched data.
- Show "al {asOf}" at 11px or larger with sufficient contrast.
