- Add an amber "desactualizado" badge when the data is older than one release cycle: more than 3 business days for daily rates, 8 days for CETES, 20 days for INPC, 100 days for GDP. Add a gray "ref. fija" badge when `fallback` is true.
- Put the tasa objetivo and TIIE de fondeo first. Add CETES 28/91/364 and Bono M 10Y, plus a derived ex-post real rate (CETES 28 minus annual INPC), clearly labeled.
- Label the GDP basis (t/t a.e. vs a/a).
- Optionally show tasa objetivo, CETES 28 and INPC in the top strip, each with its as-of date.

findings.title: Losses rendered without a minus sign; color is the only cue, and the rebalance sell instruction looks like a buy
findings.evidence: Rebalance Δ: `${delta > 0 ? "+" : ""}${fmt(Math.abs(delta))}`, so selling 5 shares shows '5.000' in red. DataRow: `{up ? "+" : ""}{Math.abs(pct).toFixed(2)}%`. Indicadores Principales: `{up ? "+" : ""}{Math.abs(d.pct).toFixed(2)}%`. A -1.20% move displays as '1.20%'.
findings.why: This fails WCAG 1.4.1 Use of Color (Level A). About 8% of men have red/green color deficiency. In the rebalance table it can reverse a trade instruction. Financial convention is to always show the sign.
findings.fix: Create one formatter, e.g. `fmtPct = new Intl.NumberFormat('es-MX',{style:'percent',minimumFractionDigits:2,signDisplay:'exceptZero'})`, and use U+2212 for the minus. For rebalancing, render 'Comprar 5' / 'Vender 5' with the MXN amount, not a bare delta.
findings.verify_reasoning:
I checked all three cited sites in /Users/luisalfredolizarragasanchez/Desktop/CLAUDE/05 NEWKAIZEN/src/App.jsx. The code does what the finding says.

1) Rebalance table, lines 2898-2905. The delta is computed at line 2785 as `const delta = tShares !== null ? tShares - currentShares : null`, so a negative value means sell. Share rows render `${delta > 0 ? "+" : ""}${fmt(Math.abs(delta))}`. The local `fmt` (line 2573) gives 5.toFixed(3) = "5.000". So selling 5 shares shows "5.000" in var(--negative) red, under the column header "Δ acciones" (line 2773). Nothing else on the row says buy or sell. An unsigned number under a delta header normally reads as positive, so the text states the wrong sign, not just the wrong color. The $MXN cash row directly above (line 2904) already uses "−" (U+2212). That shows the missing sign on share rows is an oversight and not a design choice.

2) DataRow, line 3775: `{up ? "+" : ""}{Math.abs(pct).toFixed(2)}%`. This component is used for IPC, 10Y, DXY and others at lines 4051-4129. A pct of -1.20 renders as "1.20%" in red.

3) Indicadores Principales grid, line 3917: the same pattern with `Math.abs(d.pct)`.

Extra evidence that these are bugs: the badge at line 3869 in the same view renders `{up ? "+" : ""}{d.change_pct.toFixed(2)}%` without Math.abs, so its sign is correct. The unused MktCard (lines 599/624) pairs Math.abs with ▲/▼ glyphs, which is a non-color cue. The three cited sites have neither a sign nor a glyph.

Nuance: positive values do carry a "+", so there is a weak text cue (the "+" is there or it isn't). That makes a strict WCAG 1.4.1 failure arguable. But the bigger problem is that the text of every negative value is simply wrong. Severity high is justified for the rebalance column, because it is an instruction users act on and the sign flip can reverse it. The two market-data sites alone would be medium-high.

Out of scope and acceptable: lines 646-673 use Math.abs with verbs (avanza/retrocede, sube/baja). Line 3033 shows an unsigned pnlPct in parentheses right after a signed pnl.

Corrections to the proposed fix:
(a) `Intl.NumberFormat` with style:'percent' multiplies by 100, so you would call `fmtPct.format(pct/100)`, because pct here is already in percent units.
(b) The es-MX locale formats a minus as a hyphen-minus, not U+2212. Its percent pattern may also differ from the app's en-US grouping (used everywhere, e.g. toLocaleString("en-US")). The simplest consistent fix is the pattern the app already uses at lines 2904 and 3032.
findings.corrected_fix: Add one shared helper near the top of src/App.jsx and use it at all three sites: ```js const signed = (n, dec = 2) => n == null || isNaN(n) ? "—" : (n > 0 ? "+" : n < 0 ? "−" : "") + Math.abs(n).toFixed(dec); const fmtChgPct = (p) => p == null ? "—" : signed(p, 2) + "%"; ``` - Line 3775 (DataRow): replace `{up ? "+" : ""}{Math.abs(pct).toFixed(2)}%` with `{fmtChgPct(pct)}`. Optionally add a glyph as a non-color cue: `{up ? "▲" : "▼"} ` with aria-hidden, and add an aria-label such as `sube 1.20%` / `baja 1.20%`. - Line 3917 (Indicadores Principales): replace with `{fmtChgPct(d.pct)}`. - Lines 2903-2905 (rebalance): change the header at line 2773 from "Δ acciones" to "Acción". For non-cash rows, render a verb, the share quantity and the MXN amount, using `priceMXN`, which is already in scope at line 2782: ```jsx {delta > 0 ? "Comprar " : "Vender "}{fmt(Math.abs(delta))} · ${(Math.abs(delta)*priceMXN).toLocaleString("en-US",{maximumFractionDigits:0})} ``` Keep the green/red color as a secondary cue only. Make the $MXN row say "Aportar $X" / "Retirar $X" instead of the signed amount. Optional: drop Math.abs+sign concatenation throughout and use `Intl.NumberFormat("en-US",{minimumFractionDigits:2,maximumFractionDigits:2,signDisplay:"exceptZero"})`, remembering that style:"percent" would need pct/100. Then swap "-" for "−" if you want typographic minus.

findings.title: MetricBadge paints every ROE, margin, revenue-growth and beta value red, and negative P/E green
findings.evidence: `if (good !== undefined && v <= good) positive; else if (neutral !== undefined && v <= neutral) warning; else if (!isNaN(v)) color = "var(--negative)"`. ROE%, Margen%, Rev.G% and Beta are passed without thresholds, so any number, including a 150% ROE, turns red. A loss-maker's P/E of -8 passes `v <= 20` and turns green. The Análisis metrics repeat this with `lo: v => v < 15` for P/E.
findings.why: Red and green are read as good and bad. Right now strong fundamentals look alarming and unprofitable companies look cheap.
findings.fix: Add a `direction: 'higher'|'lower'|'none'` param. ROE ≥15 green, 8–15 amber, <8 red. Margin ≥15/5. Growth >10/0. Beta gets no color. For P/E ≤0 show 'N/A · pérdidas' in muted. Show D/E as a ratio or with '%' (yfinance debtToEquity is a percentage; the Balance table at 5045 labels it 'x').
findings.verify_reasoning:
The main claim holds. The negative-P/E example and the claim that Análisis repeats the bug do not hold as written.

CONFIRMED, MetricBadge (src/App.jsx:413-420): the logic is `if (good !== undefined && v <= good) positive; else if (neutral !== undefined && v <= neutral) warning; else if (!isNaN(v)) negative`. At 3072-3074 and 3076, ROE%, Margen%, Rev.G% and Beta are passed with no `good` or `neutral`. So every finite value lands in the last branch and turns red. A 40% ROE, a 25% margin, 30% revenue growth and a 0.8 beta all show as alarming. The badge also only understands "lower is better". It has no way to express "higher is better", which ROE, margin and growth need. Beta is a measure of systematic risk, not a quality score, so it should get no good/bad color.

WEAK, the P/E = -8 example: P/E comes from backend.py:312-315. It is `price/eps` only when `eps_val > 0`. Otherwise it falls back to Yahoo's `trailingPE`, and Yahoo normally omits that field for loss-makers. A negative P/E is therefore rare in this payload. The same "any negative multiple passes `v <= good`" flaw is real for other fields, though:
- EV/EBITDA (3067): `enterpriseToEbitda` from Yahoo can be negative when EBITDA is negative. backend.py:317 only guards the fallback path, not the Yahoo value.
- P/B (3068): `priceToBook` from Yahoo can be negative when book equity is negative.
- D/E (3075): a negative `debtToEquity` from negative equity would also turn green.
So the "cheap-looking loss-maker" point stands, but it applies mainly to EV/EBITDA and P/B, not P/E.

OVERSTATED, the Análisis metrics (5001-5008): they do not repeat the all-red bug. They use `lo`/`hi` predicates. ROE only turns red when below 0 (`hi: v => v < 0`), margin when below 5, beta and ROE have no `lo`, and everything else shows white (5299-5302). What does repeat is the negative-multiple problem. `lo: v => v < 15` (P/E), `v < 10` (EV/EBITDA), `v < 2` (P/B) and `v < 50` (D/E) all paint negative values with the accent color. Minor point: strong ROE or margin is never shown as good there.

CONFIRMED, D/E units: yfinance `debtToEquity` is a percentage. The backend fallback at backend.py:294-295 also multiplies by 100, and the 80/150 and 50/200 thresholds are consistent with a percentage. But 3075 and 5008 show a bare number labeled "D/E", and 5045 labels it `unit: "x"`. A 150% D/E therefore displays as "150.00 x", which overstates leverage 100-fold.

Severity: the numbers themselves are correct and only the colors mislead. Still, it hits every position's fundamentals panel. High is defensible, and medium-high is more precise.
findings.corrected_fix:
1) Rewrite MetricBadge (src/App.jsx:413-420) as `function MetricBadge({ label, value, good, neutral, dir = 'lower', suffix = '' })`:
- If `v` is NaN, or `dir === 'none'`, use muted.
- If `dir === 'lower'` (valuation multiples) and `v <= 0`, show `value` in muted with `title="No significativo: utilidad/EBITDA/capital negativo"`. Optionally append " n.s.".

findings.title: The same '$' means USD in position cards and MXN in the summary; no currency labels or thousands separators
findings.evidence: Cards: `const value = price ? pos.shares * price : null; const cost_total = pos.shares * pos.cost;` in native currency, shown as `$${value.toFixed(2)}` (e.g. '$12345.67', no separators). The summary shows `Valor total · MXN $…`. The Análisis header shows `$${f.price}` and `Cap $${(f.marketCap/1e9).toFixed(1)}B` without currency. posCostMXN converts USD cost at today's FX, so the FX effect since purchase is never shown.
findings.why: For a Mexican user '$' defaults to pesos, so a US$ P&L shown as '$' is off by roughly 17x in their head. Mixed units in the same view break comparability, and 'B' is ambiguous in Spanish, where billón means 10^12.
findings.fix: Add `fmtMoney(v, ccy)` using Intl.NumberFormat('es-MX',{style:'currency',currency:ccy,currencyDisplay:'code'}) and show 'US$' / 'MX$' explicitly. In each card, show native value plus an MXN line. Label the cost input 'Costo promedio (USD)' when the ticker has no .MX suffix. Use 'mil M' / 'MM' instead of 'B'. Store the FX rate at purchase so P&L can be split into price effect and FX effect.
findings.verify_reasoning:
The main point is right. Some of the evidence is wrong or overstated, and the most serious problem is one the finding only mentions in passing.

CONFIRMED:
- Position cards use native currency with no label. Lines 2995-2999 compute `value = pos.shares * price` and `cost_total = pos.shares * pos.cost` with raw `sd.price`, which is USD for any ticker without `.MX` because `isMXN` at line 15 only checks the suffix.
- These values are shown as `$${price.toFixed(2)}` (3027), `$${Math.abs(pnl).toFixed(2)}` (3032) and in the Costo/acc, Invertido, Valor actual and P&L cells (3046-3049). There is no currency marker and no thousands separator, so you get "$12345.67".
- The summary block just above uses the same "$" for MXN: "Valor total · MXN" and "Costo total · MXN" at 2731-2736, and "P&L ($)" at 2737 is also MXN. So one screen mixes USD and MXN under the same symbol.
- The inconsistency even shows up inside a single card. The valuation sub-block labels its currency (`cur = d.priceCurrency`, lines 3096, 3111, 3117, 3145), but the P&L grid above it does not.
- The cost input at 2486-2489 is labeled only "COSTO PROMEDIO" (aria-label "Costo promedio por acción") with no currency. A GBM/SIC user who paid in pesos for AAPL will likely type a peso cost next to a USD price, which gives a nonsense P&L.
- The Análisis header (5181, 5191) has no currency, and "Cap $…B" uses "B", which is ambiguous in Spanish (billón = 10^12). The backend already returns `currency` from `/stock` (backend.py:437), and the FIBRA view already shows it (App.jsx 4639, 4700). So this is simply an omission.
- FX effect: `posCostMXN` (lines 22-24) converts the USD cost at today's `usdMxn`. The card labeled "Costo total · MXN" is therefore not the historical MXN cost; it is the USD cost converted at today's rate. The MXN P&L (2528) and P&L % (2529) contain no currency gain or loss. The % is really a USD return. Nothing stores the purchase exchange rate: no fx/costFx field exists, and positions are `{ticker, shares, cost}` at 2021/2025.
  - Example: bought at 17, now 20. A Mexican investor's MXN return is (1+r_usd)(1.176)−1, but the app shows r_usd. That understates or overstates the return that matters for their spending currency and for SAT's MXN-based ISR gain.
  - This number is labeled wrong, and it justifies keeping "high" severity more than the missing "$" label does.

WRONG OR OVERSTATED:
- The Análisis price at 5181 is not a raw `$${f.price}`. It uses `toLocaleString("en-US", {min/maxFractionDigits:2})`, so it has separators. Only the currency label is missing.
- 2597 (donut tooltip, `posVal`) and 2628 (donut center, `totalValue`) are MXN, the same currency as the summary. They are unlabeled but they are not USD-vs-MXN mixing, and a Mexican user reads "$" as pesos correctly there. They are weak evidence for the "same $ means USD" claim.
- "No thousands separators" is true only for the cards. The summary (2732-2737) and the donut (2597) use `toLocaleString`.
- The suggested fix with `currencyDisplay:'code'` renders "USD 1,234.56" / "MXN 1,234.56", not "US$" / "MX$" as the finding says. Either works, but the finding contradicts itself.
- Inferring currency from the `.MX` suffix, as the finding suggests, is itself fragile: `.TO` would be treated as USD instead of CAD, and `.T` as USD instead of JPY. Use the backend `currency` field.

EXTRA ISSUE (related): `usdMxn` starts at 17.5 (1090, 125). If `/fx` fails, the `.catch(() => {})` at 1237 hides it, so every MXN figure uses a hard-coded rate. The only sign is the "USD/MXN 17.50" pill at 2696.

Severity: high still holds, but mainly for the FX/cost-basis mislabeling. The missing symbols on the cards alone would be medium.
findings.corrected_fix:

findings.title: '+ Agregar' on an existing ticker silently replaces the position; a missing cost gives '+Infinity%' P&L
findings.evidence: `if (portfolio.find(p => p.ticker === t)) setPortfolio(prev => prev.map(p => p.ticker === t ? { ...p, shares, cost: ... } : p))`, so shares are replaced, not added. A new position without a cost gets `cost: isNaN(cost) ? 0 : cost`, then `pnlPct = (pnl / cost_total) * 100` with cost_total=0.
findings.why: A user logging an extra purchase loses the original lot and its cost basis without any warning. A 0 cost basis inflates P&L to 100% of market value and displays 'Infinity%'.
findings.fix: When the ticker already exists, ask '¿Sumar a la posición o reemplazar?'. For 'sumar', compute weighted average cost (s1·c1+s2·c2)/(s1+s2). Make cost required, or mark it 'Sin costo' and hide P&L. Guard every division by cost. Confirm with a toast such as 'Se agregaron 10 AAPL a Principal'.
findings.verify_reasoning:
The core of the finding holds, but some details and the fix need correcting.

1) Replace vs. add. In /Users/luisalfredolizarragasanchez/Desktop/CLAUDE/05 NEWKAIZEN/src/App.jsx lines 2019-2023, when the ticker already exists the code runs `setPortfolio(prev => prev.map(p => p.ticker === t ? { ...p, shares, cost: t === '$MXN' ? 1 : isNaN(cost) ? p.cost : cost } : p))`. The old share count is overwritten, not added to. The button always reads "+ Agregar" (line 2489). There is no confirmation and no success message; the app has no toast component at all. So the silent replace is confirmed. Three corrections to the finding:
- The cost basis is not always lost. If the cost field is left blank, the old per-share `p.cost` is kept and applied to the new share count. That is still a wrong basis whenever the new lot was bought at a different price. If a cost is typed, it replaces the old one.
- The field is labeled "COSTO PROMEDIO" (line 2485). That hints the form was built as "set total shares at average cost", which works correctly if the user types the total shares and the blended cost. The "+ Agregar" label contradicts that.
- In "%" mode (lines 1990-2013), replacing is the right behavior. The user is setting a target weight, so the shares are computed from pct × budget. The "sumar o reemplazar" choice only fits "#" (shares) mode.

2) Zero cost. A new position with a blank cost gets `cost: isNaN(cost) ? 0 : cost` (line 2025). Negative values and 0 also pass, because only NaN is checked. On the card (lines 2997-2999), `cost_total = pos.shares * pos.cost` becomes 0, `pnl = value - 0` equals the full market value, and `pnlPct = (pnl / cost_total) * 100` is Infinity. That shows as "(Infinity%)" in the header (line 3033, `Math.abs(pnlPct).toFixed(2)`) and "+Infinity%" in the P&L (%) tile (line 3050). Confirmed. This path is common: in "%" mode, users often build hypothetical portfolios without entering a cost.

The finding misses the portfolio-level effect. Lines 2511-2529 and 2737-2738 compute `totalPnl = totalValue - totalCost`, so the full market value of a zero-cost position is counted as profit in the headline total P&L. `totalPnlPct` is protected against dividing by zero (`totalCost ? ... : 0`), but it is inflated when other positions have a cost. If every position has no cost, it shows +0.00% next to a large positive P&L. This is the more misleading number, because it is the headline one.

Severity: high is reasonable, mainly because of the inflated total P&L and the silent overwrite of share counts. The Infinity% display is obviously broken but less likely to mislead anyone.
findings.corrected_fix:
All changes are in src/App.jsx.

(a) addStock (lines 1979-2033):
- Validate cost: `if (!isNaN(cost) && cost <= 0) { setAddError('El costo debe ser > 0'); return; }`.
- In '#' (shares) mode, when the ticker already exists (line 2019), ask the user to choose "Sumar a la posición" or "Reemplazar". An inline two-button choice is better than window.confirm.
- For "Sumar":
  - `newShares = p.shares + shares`
  - `newCost = isNaN(cost) ? p.cost : (p.shares*p.cost + shares*cost)/newShares` (weighted average cost; both lots are priced in the ticker's own currency, so no FX conversion is needed)
  - If p.cost is 0 or unknown, keep the position marked as "no cost".
- For "Reemplazar", keep the current behavior.
- In '%' mode, keep replace semantics (target weight), but rename the button "Actualizar %" when the ticker already exists.
- For $MXN, "Sumar" should add the cash amount.
- Rename the button dynamically: "+ Agregar" for new tickers, "Actualizar" for existing ones.

(b) Missing cost:
- In '%' mode, default the cost to the current price (`cost = price`), so a hypothetical position starts at P&L 0, which is economically correct for a new model allocation.
- In '#' mode, either require the cost or store `cost: null` instead of 0.

(c) Card (lines 2996-2999, 3033, 3046-3050):
- `const hasCost = pos.cost > 0;`
- `cost_total = hasCost ? pos.shares*pos.cost : null`
- `pnl = hasCost && value != null ? value - cost_total : null`
- `pnlPct = pnl != null && cost_total > 0 ? pnl/cost_total*100 : null`
- Show "Sin costo" for Costo/acc and Invertido when there is no cost.
- As a safety net, render P&L % only when `Number.isFinite(pnlPct)`.

(d) Totals (lines 2511-2529):
- Build totalValue and totalCost only from positions with `cost > 0`: `totalPnl = Σ(val − cost)` over costed positions and `totalPnlPct = totalCost > 0 ? totalPnl/totalCost*100 : null`.
- Keep total market value across all positions.
- Add the note "N posiciones sin costo excluidas del P&L" and show "—" instead of "+0.00%" when totalPnlPct is null.

(e) Add a success message, e.g. a transient green line next to the form (the add form already shows errors via addError): "Se agregaron 10 AAPL a <portfolio name> · costo prom. $X", or "Posición AAPL reemplazada".

findings.title: An invalid ticker never shows an error; its card says 'Cargando...' forever
findings.evidence:
loadStockData: `const sd = await fetchStock(ticker); if (sd) setStockData(...)`. A null result, e.g. for 'APPL', is dropped. The card renders `price != null ? … :
Cargando...
`. Shares mode adds the ticker without validating it. The Sharpe KPI likewise shows 'calculando…' whenever the value is null, including after failure.
findings.why: Users can't tell a typo from a slow server. The card and portfolio totals stay incomplete, and targetPcts never initialize because `allPricesLoaded` is never true (1202-1203).
findings.fix: Validate via /stock before adding in every mode. Track per-ticker status {loading|ok|error}. The error card should say 'No encontramos APPL. ¿Quisiste decir AAPL? · Reintentar · Eliminar'. Add ticker autocomplete through a backend search endpoint and remind users about the .MX suffix for BMV and SIC listings.
findings.verify_reasoning:
The main claim holds: a mistyped ticker never produces an error, and its card shows "Cargando..." forever. Three details are wrong or missing.

1. **Why APPL gets stuck (the finding's explanation is wrong).** The backend always answers HTTP 200 (backend.py:1917). For a ticker that passes the format check but doesn't exist, like APPL, get_stock (backend.py:179-437) does not raise an error. It returns a full dict with `"price": r2(None)` → null, `name` = the ticker itself, and no `error` key. fetchStock (App.jsx:111, `return data?.error ? null : data`) passes that dict through, and loadStockData (App.jsx:1258-1259) stores `stockData['APPL'] = {price:null, name:'APPL', ...}`. So the result is not "null and dropped"; it is saved. Because `stockData[t]` is now set, loadAll (1276) never tries again. `setLoading(false)` hides the spinner, but the card still falls into `price != null ? ... : "Cargando..."` (3026-3028). The result is a static "Cargando..." with no spinner. Only tickers that fail the format check (`_TICKER_RE`, backend.py:1866) or throw an exception come back as `{error}` and give null. A network failure after 3 tries is caught at 1263 and only logged to the console. Every path ends the same way.

2. **Adding a ticker.** Confirmed. Shares mode, which is the default (`useState("shares")`, 1145), adds with no check (2015-2026). Percent mode does check (2011). But its message, "No se pudo obtener el precio actual. Intenta en modo Acciones.", sends the user to the one mode that skips the check.

3. **Target percentages.** Confirmed. `allPricesLoaded = portfolio.every(p => stockData[p.ticker]?.price)` (1202) is never true, so targetPcts never initialize in normal mode. Experimental mode is not affected.

4. **Sharpe (the finding is partly wrong).** A bad ticker does not leave the KPI stuck on "calculando…". In loadSharpeData (1815-1858), fetchChart returns [] for APPL, the `closes.length < 10` check skips it, and the Sharpe ratio is computed on the other tickers with their weights rescaled. Nothing tells the user APPL was left out. "calculando…" (2742) only stays forever when every chart fails, for example when the backend is down or all tickers are bad. That is still a real problem, because failure looks the same as loading.

5. **Missing and more serious: the totals are wrong.** posValMXN returns 0 when there is no price (19), but totalCost still adds `posCost(p)` for the bad position (2517). The portfolio P&L therefore shows a false loss equal to that position's full cost basis. The position also silently drops out of total value, the pie chart and the weights. That alone justifies high severity.

Minor points: "¿Quisiste decir AAPL?" needs a search endpoint, which the backend doesn't have. For a typo, the backend also spends time on info retries with sleeps and financial-statement fetches before returning an empty result.
findings.corrected_fix:
1. **Backend (backend.py get_stock, around line 208).** After the price fallbacks, if `price is None and not info`, return `{"error": "not_found", "ticker": ticker}` right away. Don't fetch financial statements for a ticker that doesn't exist. Better still, return HTTP 404 for not_found (do_GET currently always sends 200).

2. **fetchStock (App.jsx:105-120).** Treat `data?.error === 'not_found' || data?.price == null` as not found: return `{notFound:true}` or throw a typed NotFoundError. Keep network and timeout errors separate, since they already throw after retries.

3. **Per-ticker status.** Add `const [tickerStatus, setTickerStatus] = useState({})` with values 'loading' | 'ok' | 'notfound' | 'neterror', set in loadStockData (1251-1267). Never write a price-less record into stockData.

4. **Card (3026-3028).**
   - 'loading' → spinner plus "Cargando…".
   - 'notfound' → "No encontramos {ticker}." plus a hint when the ticker has no '.': "Si cotiza en la BMV/SIC, prueba {ticker}.MX". Show buttons [Eliminar] (removeStock) and [Editar].
   - 'neterror' → "Sin conexión con el servidor" plus [Reintentar], which clears the status and calls loadStockData.

5. **addStock (1980-2033).** In every mode, call fetchStock before adding anything except $MXN. On not found, `setAddError(`No encontramos ${t}. ¿Es de la BMV? Prueba ${t}.MX`)` and do not add. On a network error, show "El servidor está despertando; intenta de nuevo" and do not add, or add with a visible warning. Remove the "Intenta en modo Acciones" advice at 2011.

6. **Totals and P&L (2510-2530).** Leave positions with no price out of both totalValue and totalCost. Show a banner: "N posición(es) sin precio excluidas del total: APPL".

7. **Target percentages (1202).** Check only tickers whose status is not 'notfound': `portfolio.filter(p => tickerStatus[p.ticker] !== 'notfound').every(p => stockData[p.ticker]?.price)`.

8. **Sharpe (1815-1858, 2740-2742).** Track `sharpeStatus` ('running' | 'ok' | 'error') and the list of skipped tickers. Show "calculando…" only while a run is in progress. Show "Sin datos · Reintentar" when no ticker produced a result, and "Excluye: APPL (sin histórico)" when some were skipped.

9. **Optional:** ticker autocomplete through a new /search endpoint (yfinance Search or the Yahoo search API) to power the "¿Quisiste decir AAPL?" suggestion.

findings.title: Destructive actions have no confirmation or undo (delete portfolio, delete position, apply rebalance)
findings.evidence: The 14px '×' next to each portfolio runs `const next = portfolios.filter(x => x.id !== p.id); setPortfolios(next); savePortfolios(next);` right away. 'Eliminar' on a card calls removeStock immediately. 'Aplicar rebalanceo' overwrites every position's shares (`{ ...x, shares: newShares }`), keeps the old average cost, and gives no preview.
findings.why: The only storage is localStorage, so one mis-tap permanently destroys user data (Nielsen heuristic #3, user control and freedom; #5, error prevention).
findings.fix: Portfolio delete: a modal that names the portfolio and its position count. Position delete and rebalance: an 8-second 'Deshacer' toast that keeps a snapshot of the previous state. Rebalance: show a trade-list preview (Comprar/Vender, acciones, monto MXN) before applying.
findings.verify_reasoning:
The main point holds. One claim, that rebalance gives no preview, is wrong.

Confirmed in the code:
- Portfolio delete, src/App.jsx:2359-2369. The × button runs `portfolios.filter(x => x.id !== p.id); setPortfolios(next); savePortfolios(next);` straight away, with no confirm. It is a 14px glyph with `padding: "0 2px"`, sitting right next to the 12px ⧉ duplicate button (2348-2358). Two tiny targets side by side make a mis-tap more likely.
- Position delete, 3170-3173. 'Eliminar' calls `removeStock(pos.ticker)` (2035-2043). That filters the position out through `setPortfolio`, which persists at once (`savePortfolios` inside the updater, 1063-1073). It also deletes that ticker's `targetPcts`.
- Rebalance apply, 2918-2936. It overwrites every row with `{ ...x, shares: newShares }`, keeps `x.cost` unchanged and clears `customTotal`.
- Storage is only localStorage (`savePortfolios`, 813-815). A grep of App.jsx and ui.jsx finds no undo, no toast, no `confirm(`, and no export/import of portfolios. The only Blob download is the EDGAR CSV at 85-98. So one mis-tap permanently destroys data, including cost basis, which the user cannot get back. Citing Nielsen #3 and #5 is correct.

Where the finding is wrong:
- The rebalance screen already has a per-row preview. The table (2760-2907) has 'Acciones' (target shares `tShares`) and 'Δ acciones' columns, with +/− coloring. It uses the same base as apply: `effTotal = customTotal || totalValue` at 2572, and apply uses `customTotal || effTotal` at 2923. So "no preview" is false, and a separate trade-list modal would mostly repeat that table.
- What is actually missing: a MXN amount per trade, Comprar/Vender labels, a summary of total bought and sold, and any way to undo.

What the finding understates:
- Keeping the old average cost is not only a UX problem. It is a cost-basis bug. Under the average-cost method, buying more shares must blend the old cost with the new purchase price. Selling leaves the per-share cost unchanged. The code never blends on buys, so every later P&L figure is wrong: 'Costo total' at 2736, `cost_total = pos.shares * pos.cost` at 2997, and 'Costo/acc' at 3046.

Severity: high is fair for portfolio delete, since one click wipes every position and its cost basis. Position delete alone is closer to medium.
findings.corrected_fix:
1) Portfolio delete (App.jsx:2359-2369). Put a confirm dialog in front of the delete: "¿Eliminar «{p.name}» y sus {p.positions.length} posiciones? No se puede deshacer." It needs a destructive 'Eliminar' button and a 'Cancelar' button that has default focus. Also make the × a real target of at least 24px (WCAG 2.5.8) and put a gap between it and the ⧉ button. Use a functional update so the list is never stale: `setPortfolios(prev => { const next = prev.filter(x => x.id !== p.id); savePortfolios(next); return next; })`. Then fix `activePortfolioId`.

2) Undo for position delete and rebalance. Before either change, save a snapshot keyed by portfolio id, not by whichever portfolio is active later: `const snap = { pid: activePortfolioId, positions: structuredClone(portfolio), targetPcts: { ...targetPcts } }`. Show an 8-second toast ('AAPL eliminada · Deshacer' or 'Rebalanceo aplicado · Deshacer'). Undo should run `setPortfolios(prev => { const next = prev.map(p => p.id === snap.pid ? { ...p, positions: snap.positions } : p); savePortfolios(next); return next; })` and restore `setTargetPcts(snap.targetPcts)`. For rebalance, also restore `customTotal`. The toast needs `role="status"`/`aria-live="polite"`. Use only one pending undo slot, and replace it on each new action.

3) Rebalance. Keep the existing table (2760-2907) and add to it rather than building a new preview:
- A 'Monto MXN' column: `delta * priceMXN`.
- A Comprar/Vender label per row.
- A footer summary above the 'Aplicar rebalanceo' button: "Compras $X · Ventas $Y · N operaciones".

4) Fix cost basis in the apply handler (2924-2933), using the average-cost method. `x.cost` and `price` are both in the ticker's own currency:
```
const oldSh = x.shares || 0;
const d = newShares - oldSh;
const cost = x.ticker === '$MXN' ? 1
  : (d > 0 && newShares > 0) ? (oldSh * (x.cost || 0) + d * price) / newShares
  : x.cost;
return { ...x, shares: newShares, cost };
```
Also drop positions where `newShares === 0`, or keep them on purpose.

5) Add export/import of `momentum_portfolios` as JSON. The only store is localStorage, so this is the only protection against clearing the browser or switching devices.

findings.title: On mobile (≤768px) users can't log out or see connection/RF status, and the bottom nav is a hidden-scrollbar strip of 8 text pills
findings.evidence: `.app-sidebar { display: none; }` at max-width 768 and `.app-menu-button { display: none; }`. The Menu and X icons are imported (App.jsx:7) but never rendered. Logout exists only in the sidebar (App.jsx:2212). Bottom nav buttons use `padding:"8px 16px", fontSize:12`, about 31px tall, with no icons, the scrollbar hidden via `scrollbar-width: none`, and color #9aada3 hardcoded.
findings.why: At 390px only about 4 of 8 tabs are visible, with no hint that more exist. Touch targets are under 44px (Apple HIG and Material both recommend 44-48px). Session control is missing on the device most people will use. Also, `html, body { overflow-x:hidden }` (App.jsx:2116) turns body into a scroll container, which typically breaks the sticky topbar.
findings.fix: Use a 5-slot icon and label tab bar at least 56px tall (Mercados, Portafolio, Buscar, Ideas, Más). Put the remaining tools plus theme, status, RF rate and 'Cerrar sesión' in a 'Más' bottom sheet, or wire up the existing .app-menu-button as a drawer. Remove the global overflow-x hack and fix the actual overflow sources.
findings.verify_reasoning:
The main claims hold up. Four supporting details are wrong or overstated.

CONFIRMED:
(1) Logout is only in the sidebar. onLogout is used only at App.jsx:1041 (where it is defined), 1044 (the prop) and 2212 (the sidebar Button). theme.css:261 hides `.app-sidebar` at max-width 768. The session flag is saved in localStorage (App.jsx:52-59, `localStorage.setItem(AUTH_KEY,"1")`) and does not expire, so a phone user has no way to end the session except clearing site data. That matters on shared devices, and the owner wants to hand this to company employees. High severity is justified.
(2) Backend connection status (`backendOk`) is shown only at App.jsx:2199-2205, which is inside the hidden sidebar.
(3) `Menu` and `X` are imported at App.jsx:7 but never rendered. Grepping for <X, <Menu and {X} finds nothing.
(4) The bottom nav (App.jsx:2271-2293) is 8 text-only pills with `padding:"8px 16px", fontSize:12`. theme.css:99 applies `font: inherit`, which gives line-height normal, so each pill is about 31px tall. The scrollbar is hidden (theme.css:267-270) and there are no icons. At 390px, Noticias, Portfolio, Sharpe and ML Screener fit (about 355px), Analytics is partly cut off, and FIBRAs, Fórmula Mágica and Análisis are off-screen.
(5) The sticky-topbar claim is correct. App.jsx:2116 sets `html, body { overflow-x:hidden }`. Because html's overflow goes to the viewport, body's own overflow-x:hidden makes body a scroll container (overflow-y becomes auto). Body grows with its content (theme.css:98 sets only min-height), so it never scrolls itself. The sticky `.app-topbar` (theme.css:253) is measured against body, so it never sticks on mobile.

WRONG OR OVERSTATED:
(a) "Can't see RF status" is partly wrong. The risk-free rate is shown where it is used: in the Sharpe tab at App.jsx:3205 (`Tasa libre de riesgo: …(rfLabel)`), 3313 and 3579. Only the global sidebar badge is missing.
(b) The hardcoded `#9aada3` is not a defect. `--bg-deep` is dark in both themes (theme.css:7 `#11251c`, :51 `#07100b`). The sidebar is intentionally dark in both themes (theme.css:342-387), and `.app-nav-link` uses the same `#9aada3` (theme.css:245). Contrast on #11251c is well above 4.5:1. A token would be cleaner, but this is not a bug.
(c) "Wire up the existing .app-menu-button" is misleading. Only the CSS rule exists (theme.css:255); no element in App.jsx or ui.jsx uses that class.
(d) The touch-target point is valid against Apple HIG (44pt) and Material (48dp). But about 31px still passes WCAG 2.2 AA 2.5.8, which requires 24x24 CSS px. It fails only the AAA 2.5.5 level (44px). "No hint that more exist" is also overstated: the cut-off 5th pill is a weak scroll hint, though a poor one.
Also, the top bar on mobile shows the current tab name twice: once in the breadcrumb (2224-2235) and again in `.mobile-tab-label` (2258-2265).
findings.corrected_fix:
1) Replace the bottom strip (App.jsx:2271-2293) with a fixed 5-slot tab bar: `<nav aria-label="Navegación principal" className="bottom-nav-mobile">`. Each slot is a button with a lucide icon (size 20) above a 10-11px label, `min-height:56px`, `flex:1`, and `aria-current="page"` on the active tab. Suggested slots: Portfolio (Briefcase), Noticias (Newspaper), Análisis (LineChartIcon), Screener (ListFilter), Más (Menu). In theme.css:262-272, drop `overflow-x:auto` and the scrollbar-hiding rules, and use `display:grid; grid-template-columns:repeat(5,1fr)`. Also add `viewport-fit=cover` to the viewport meta in index.html; otherwise `env(safe-area-inset-bottom)` returns 0 on iOS standalone and the bar can sit under the home indicator.

2) "Más" opens a bottom sheet (`role="dialog"`, `aria-modal`, closed with X, Escape or a backdrop tap, focus trapped). It contains the remaining tabs (Analytics vs SPY, Sharpe Optimizer, FIBRA Screener, Fórmula Mágica), the ThemeToggle, the backend status pill, the RF badge (`rfLabel` + `(rfRate*100).toFixed(2)%`) and a "Cerrar sesión" button that calls `onLogout`. The simplest way is to move the sidebar-foot block (App.jsx:2198-2215) into a small `<SessionFooter/>` component and render it in both the sidebar and the sheet, so the two cannot drift apart. The currently unused `Menu` and `X` imports become the Más and close icons. Alternatively, add a real `<IconButton className="app-menu-button">` to the topbar that opens the sidebar as an off-canvas drawer, and set `.app-menu-button{display:inline-flex}` inside the 768px media query. Either way, delete the dead `.app-menu-button{display:none}` rule if it stays unused.

3) Delete `html, body { overflow-x:hidden; max-width:100vw; }` (App.jsx:2116) so the sticky topbar works again. Contain overflow at its sources instead: the existing `.table-scroll`, `.rebal-table-wrap` and `.corr-matrix-wrap` wrappers, plus `min-width:0` on flex/grid children. If a safety net is still needed, put `overflow-x:clip` on `.app-frame`; `clip` does not create a scroll container, so it does not break sticky.

4) On mobile, hide the duplicate breadcrumb or `.mobile-tab-label` and the macro strip in the topbar, keeping only the page title and the Más/theme controls. The macro strip can move into the sheet or onto the Noticias page.

5) Optional: replace the hardcoded `#9aada3` with a token such as `--nav-ink` defined on `.app-sidebar`/`.bottom-nav-mobile`. This is maintainability only; the color is not a contrast bug. Severity stays high because of the missing logout.

findings.title: The rule-based heuristic is sold as 'ML' with English BUY/SELL/HOLD calls and no disclaimer anywhere
findings.evidence: mlScoreStock is a set of hand-set thresholds (`pe < 12 ? 2.5 : …`, where a negative P/E also gets +2.5) ending in `const recommendation = overall_score >= 7 ? "BUY" : overall_score <= 4 ? "SELL" : "HOLD"`. The UI labels are 'ML Screener', '▶ Ejecutar ML Screener' and 'ML Score'. Grepping for 'asesor', 'no constituye', 'disclaimer' or 'aviso' finds nothing.
findings.why: Calling it machine learning overstates rigor. Unqualified buy/sell calls to Mexican retail users or employees raise CNBV investment-advice concerns and erode trust once users notice.
findings.fix: Rename to 'Puntaje KAIZEN (reglas cuantitativas)' and 'Screener cuantitativo'. Replace BUY/SELL/HOLD with 'Atractivo / Neutral / Débil' and a factor breakdown with tooltips. Add a persistent footer: 'Información con fines educativos; no constituye recomendación de inversión. Datos con retraso de ~15 min.'
findings.verify_reasoning:
The core claims hold up when checked against the code. A few details need correcting.

CONFIRMED:
1) It is a hand-tuned heuristic, not ML. At src/App.jsx:309 the code's own comment says "ML SCORER (Rule-Based Quantitative Engine)". mlScoreStock (312-393) is fixed if/else thresholds with hard-coded weights (0.22/0.28/0.18/0.18/0.14, lines 370-376). Nothing is fitted or trained. Yet users see "ML Screener" in the nav (2177, and again in the mobile/compact navs at 2230, 2261, 2274), the button reads " Ejecutar ML Screener" (3521), the Análisis card is titled "ML Score" (5317), and README.md:41 also says "ML Screener". Calling a heuristic "machine learning" overstates how rigorous and validated it is. That is a real trust and misrepresentation problem.
2) The calls are English BUY/SELL/HOLD in an otherwise Spanish UI. Line 378 sets `overall_score >= 7 ? "BUY" : overall_score <= 4 ? "SELL" : "HOLD"`. The raw value is rendered as a colored badge in the screener cards (3543, 3564) and in the Análisis pill `{score.recommendation} · {score.overall_score}/10` (5323).
3) There is no disclaimer anywhere. I grepped App.jsx, ui.jsx, main.jsx, index.html, the CSS files, README and backend.py for asesor, constituye, disclaimer, aviso, educativ, garantiz and recomendaci. The only hits are code comments and the heading "RECOMENDACIONES PARA TU PORTAFOLIO". It is worse than the finding says: the app actively claims freshness it does not have. There are "LIVE" badges (708, 977) and the copy "Datos en vivo… conectados al backend real" (985), but the data is yfinance quotes (delayed) plus fundamentals from annual or quarterly statements.

CORRECTIONS AND NUANCES:
- The negative-P/E point is true of the function but mostly doesn't happen today. `pe < 12 ? 2.5` does give +2.5 to any negative P/E. However, both callers (screener at 1720, Análisis at 4988) get data from /stock → get_stock. At backend.py:312-315 that code computes P/E only when `eps_val > 0` and otherwise falls back to Yahoo's trailingPE, which Yahoo normally leaves out for loss-making firms. PEG is also guarded (backend.py:397-403, growth > 0). So this is a missing guard, not something users routinely see. It is still worth fixing.
- The screener tab does partly disclose what the engine is. Lines 3530-3535 say "Motor cuantitativo de scoring… usando PE, PEG…". So "sold as ML" is fully true of the nav, the button and the Análisis "ML Score" card (which has no explanation). It is only partly true of the screener tab body.
- The finding misses a related problem. When a fetch fails, sd is {} (1712-1720). Every subscore then stays at its base of 5, so the stock gets "5 · HOLD" with the rationale "Datos insuficientes". A typo'd ticker gets a HOLD call based on zero data.
- The disclaimer needs to cover more than the screener. The Sharpe optimizer gives portfolio-specific actions: MANTENER/AUMENTAR/REDUCIR (3335) under "RECOMENDACIONES PARA TU PORTAFOLIO" (3436), with verdicts AGREGAR/CONSIDERAR/OMITIR (3458). Because these are tied to the user's own holdings, they look more like personalized investment advice (the kind CNBV regulates under the Ley del Mercado de Valores and its investment-services rules) than the generic screener does. A disclaimer lowers the risk but does not settle the legal question by itself.
- The fix's "~15 min" is wrong. Yahoo delays BMV (.MX) quotes by about 20 minutes, FRED/Banxico series are daily, and fundamentals can be weeks or months old. Don't state one number.
- Also relevant to the "factor breakdown" part of the fix: the weights double-count. priceChange52w drives both Momentum (18%) and Técnico (14%). ROE, margin, D/E and revenue growth each appear in both Fundamental and Calidad. P/B appears in both Valuación and Técnico. So the stated weights are not the real exposures, and a factor breakdown should show de-duplicated contributions.

Severity "high" is reasonable. The app shows retail users and employees unqualified buy/sell calls from an unvalidated heuristic labeled ML, with no disclaimer and with "LIVE" branding.
findings.corrected_fix:
1) Rename everywhere. Nav labels at src/App.jsx:2177, 2230, 2261, 2274 → "Screener cuantitativo". Button at 3521 → "Ejecutar screener". Card title at 5317 → "Puntaje KAIZEN (reglas)". Code comment at 309 and README.md:41 to match. Rename the function to quantScoreStock.
2) Replace the English calls with Spanish, non-directive labels. Line 378: `overall_score >= 7 ? "ATRACTIVO" : overall_score <= 4 ? "DÉBIL" : "NEUTRAL"`. Update the recColor checks at 3543 and 390 to use the new values.
3) Add a data-coverage gate. Count the non-null inputs among the 14 fields destructured at line 313. If fewer than about 5 are present (or the fetch failed), return `recommendation: "SIN DATOS"` and `overall_score: null`, and render "—" instead of "5 · HOLD" (3558-3566, 5323).
4) Guard the valuation math. Line 328: `if (pe != null && pe > 0) …`, and when pe is null because earnings are negative, apply an explicit loss penalty (for example val -= 1.5). Apply the same >0 guard to evEbitda (line 331), pb (line 332) and peg (line 329).
5) Show a per-factor breakdown with tooltips giving the thresholds used. Remove the double counting: priceChange52w should appear in only one sub-score (ideally 12-1 month momentum). ROE, margin and D/E should appear in either Fundamental or Calidad, not both. P/B should move out of Técnico.
6) Add a persistent footer in the app shell, near the data-status block around line 2199, plus a short line under every recommendation surface (screener cards, Análisis score card, and the optimizer tables at 3335, 3436 and 3458). Suggested text: "Información con fines educativos e informativos; no constituye asesoría ni recomendación de inversión personalizada. Puntajes generados por reglas cuantitativas fijas, no validadas estadísticamente. Cotizaciones con retraso (hasta ~20 min en BMV); datos fundamentales pueden tener semanas o meses de antigüedad. Rendimientos pasados no garantizan rendimientos futuros."
7) Remove or qualify the "LIVE" badges and the "Datos en vivo" copy (708, 977, 985). Replace them with "Datos con retraso" plus an as-of timestamp.
8) Rename the optimizer's "RECOMENDACIONES PARA TU PORTAFOLIO" to "Candidatos que mejorarían el Sharpe histórico". Change AGREGAR/OMITIR to "Mejora / Neutral / No mejora", and AUMENTAR/REDUCIR to "Peso óptimo mayor/menor (histórico)". Have Mexican counsel review whether portfolio-specific output amounts to CNBV-regulated investment advice.

findings.title: The 'Sentimiento' mood counts risk-off signals as positive, and 'LIVE' appears even without data
findings.evidence: `const positive = insights.filter(i => i.color === "var(--positive)" || i.color === "var(--warning)").length;`. Warning is used for VIX 20-30 ('volatilidad elevada, cautela'), 10Y ≤5%, gold up ('demanda de refugio'), oil up ('presión inflacionaria') and BTC up. The 'LIVE' badge renders unconditionally, and the empty state tells users to click '↻ Mercados' even though loading is automatic.
findings.why: On a risk-off day, with equities down, VIX at 25 and gold up, the summary can read 'Sentimiento: Positivo'. yfinance quotes are delayed, so 'LIVE' is inaccurate.
findings.fix: Give each insight an explicit risk sign (+1 risk-on, −1 risk-off, 0) separate from its display color, e.g. VIX>20 → −1, gold up → −1, USD/MXN up → −1. Replace 'LIVE' with 'Actualizado hh:mm · retraso ~15 min' and hide it while md is null. Fix the empty state to say 'Cargando…' or 'Sin datos · Reintentar'.
findings.verify_reasoning:
The main claims check out in src/App.jsx.

1) Mood logic. Line 687 is `insights.filter(i => i.color === "var(--positive)" || i.color === "var(--warning)")`, so every amber signal counts as positive. Amber is assigned to VIX 20–30 (line 660, with the text "volatilidad elevada, cautela recomendada"), gold up (line 672, "demanda de refugio activa") and WTI up (line 677, "presión inflacionaria"). All of those are cautionary or risk-off signals, yet each adds a positive vote.

Worked example, supply-shock day: IPC −1.5%, S&P −1.8%, USD/MXN +1.2%, VIX 26, 10Y 4.3%, gold +1.5%, WTI +4%, BTC +0.5%. That gives 5 positive votes against 3 negative, so the badge reads "Sentimiento: Positivo". With BTC down it reads "Mixto". The core claim stands.

Details the finding got wrong or left out:
(a) The finding misses the biggest built-in bias. At line 667 the 10Y is colored `r > 5 ? negative : warning`. So at any yield of 5% or less it always adds +1 to the positive count. The vote is based on the yield level, not its change, and it has nothing to do with that day's risk appetite. With FRED/^TNX near 4–4.5%, that is a permanent +1 skew.
(b) Listing BTC up as a problem is wrong. BTC is a pro-cyclical, risk-on asset, so counting BTC up as risk-on is defensible.
(c) Oil's sign is ambiguous. A supply shock pushes oil up and is risk-off; demand-driven moves are risk-on. For Mexico the effect is also two-sided (Pemex export revenue against fuel imports and the IEPS subsidy). Assigning oil up a fixed sign is not sound. Oil down is colored negative even though its text says "alivio" (line 677), which is internally inconsistent.
(d) `ins.color` is never rendered. The insight cards at lines 735–751 use `var(--accent)` for both the border and the category label, and grep finds no `ins.color`. So the colors exist only to feed the mood. The fix should replace `color` with a risk score rather than keep a separate display color.
(e) The classic demand-shock risk-off day (stocks, oil and BTC all down) correctly yields "Cauteloso". The error shows up specifically on supply-shock or inflationary risk-off days, plus the constant 10Y bias. That fits high/medium rather than a universally wrong label.

2) LIVE badge. It is hardcoded at line 708 and never gated. The data does not support it:
- backend.py lines 644–668 use `yf.download(period="5d", interval="1d")`, i.e. daily bars.
- backend.py line 704 caches results for 120 s.
- Yahoo delays data for ^MXX (about 20 min) and for CME futures GC=F/CL=F (about 10 min).
- macroData (VIX, 10Y) is fetched only once on mount (App.jsx line 1236) and never refreshed, so those two lines can be hours old.
The claim is confirmed. `lastUpdated` already exists (line 1119), is set in loadMarketData (line 1941), and is shown as "Act. hh:mm" in the hero at line 3740. It is just not passed to ResumenManero.

3) Empty state. The finding is partly right. Loading is automatic: line 1965 runs `if (!marketData) loadMarketData()` when the news tab opens, and line 1976 polls every 60 s because `autoRefresh` is hardcoded true (line 1121). The "↻ Mercados" button does exist (around line 3812), so the text works as a retry hint. The real defect is different. `loadMarketData` swallows errors (`catch {}` at line 1942), so if both /market and /macro fail, the spinner and "Cargando…" stay on screen forever with no error state.

Also, because macroData loads on mount, the panel can show a mood computed only from VIX and 10Y while md is still null. With VIX 20–30 that pair (warning + warning) reads "Positivo" before any market data exists.

Severity: the badge is a headline heuristic, not a number users trade on directly, so medium–high rather than clearly high.
findings.corrected_fix:
In ResumenManero (src/App.jsx, lines 642–690), give each insight a `risk` score and stop using color:
- IPC and S&P: risk = sign(change_pct), weight 1 each.
- USD/MXN: risk = −sign(change_pct). A weaker peso is risk-off for MX assets.
- VIX, by level: >30 → −2, 20–30 → −1, <15 → +1, else 0. If a daily change is available, add −sign(ΔVIX).
- 10Y: take it out of the vote. It is a level, not a sentiment move. If kept, use the day's change in bp and weight it 0. Show curve inversion as an info note only.
- Gold: up by more than 0.5% → −1 (safe-haven demand), else 0.
- WTI: weight 0. The sign is ambiguous (supply vs demand shock). Also fix the text/sign mismatch at line 677.
- BTC: +0.5 × sign(change_pct).

Then compute `score = Σ risk` and require at least 3 signals, including at least one equity index. Set mood = score ≥ +2 → "Risk-on", ≤ −2 → "Risk-off / Cauteloso", else "Mixto". Show a tooltip listing the contributing signals so the label can be explained.

Gate the mood badge on `md != null`, so VIX and 10Y alone never produce a mood.

Replace the hardcoded LIVE at line 708:
- Pass `lastUpdated` from the parent (line 3879: `<ResumenManero md={marketData} macroData={macroData} lastUpdated={lastUpdated} />`).
- Render `Act. {hh:mm} · datos con retraso (15–20 min)` only when `lastUpdated` is set. Hide it otherwise.
- Remove the same unconditional LIVE at line 977 as well.
- Refresh `/macro` together with loadMarketData, or label VIX/10Y with their own timestamp.

Empty state (lines 730–734):
- Add a `marketDataError` state, set in the `catch` at line 1942 (and clear it on success).
- While `marketDataLoading`, show spinner + "Cargando datos de mercado…".
- On error, or loading finished with no data, show "Sin datos de mercado · Reintentar" with a button calling loadMarketData (no spinner).

findings.title: USD/MXN direction is colored in opposite ways on the same screen
findings.evidence: Resumen: `color: up ? "var(--negative)" : "var(--positive)"` (peso weakens = red). The bento USD·MXN tile and the DataRow in 'México · Mercado' use `up ? positive : negative`, so the same move is green.
findings.why: The same number carries contradictory good/bad signals within one scroll, which undermines trust in every color on the page.
findings.fix: Pick one convention and document it: either neutral ink with an arrow for all FX, or peso-perspective coloring with an explicit label ('Peso −0.42%'). Put it in a shared <ChangePill value invert> component.

findings.title: Sharpe color scale is non-monotonic and contradicts the portfolio KPI
findings.evidence: Per stock: `s >= 1 ? positive : s >= 0.5 ? warning : s >= 0 ? "var(--accent)" : negative`, so 0.3 is green and 0.8 is amber. The portfolio KPI instead uses `>= 1 positive, >= 0.5 warning, else negative`, so 0.3 is red there.
findings.why: A worse risk-adjusted return looks better, and the same value gets different colors in two panels a few pixels apart.
findings.fix: Add one `sharpeTone(s)` helper (≥1 positive, 0.5–1 neutral/accent, 0–0.5 warning, <0 negative) and use it in Portfolio, Optimizer and Screener. Show the legend text ('≥1 excelente · 0.5–1 bueno · <0.5 bajo') at 11px or larger.

findings.title: Hardcoded colors break dark mode and fail contrast
findings.evidence: Inactive portfolio chip `"#f2f2f2"`/`"#555555"`, which becomes a light pill in dark mode. The primary '+ Agregar' button uses `background: "var(--bg-deep)"` (#07100b on #101a14 surface in dark mode, about 1.1:1). Placeholder dashes use `#ccc`, `#ddd`, `#d1d5db` (about 1.4:1 on white). Empty-state and disclaimer text uses `#374151` on bg-deep (about 1.9:1). Active-period returns use `#006633`/`#cc0000` on `#135936` (about 1.3:1). Financial tabs use white on `#3b82f6` at 12px (3.7:1). There are about 150 hex literals in total.
findings.why: These fail WCAG 1.4.3 (text 4.5:1) and 1.4.11 (UI components 3:1). The main call to action nearly disappears in dark mode.
findings.fix: Replace with tokens: chips use var(--surface-2)/var(--ink) and active var(--accent-strong)/var(--on-accent); CTAs use <Button variant="primary">; dashes use var(--muted-2); secondary text in dark panels uses var(--muted); blue uses var(--info). Add an ESLint rule (no-restricted-syntax on /#[0-9a-f]{3,6}/ in JSX style) to stop regressions.

findings.title: Keyboard focus is removed on key inputs, and key interactions are hover- or double-click-only
findings.evidence: Eleven inline `outline: "none"` styles override theme.css:110 `:focus-visible` (inline styles beat stylesheet rules). Portfolio rename works only via `onDoubleClick`, with the hint 'doble clic para renombrar' at 10px italic. The duplicate button '⧉' has only a `title`, no aria-label, and is about 12px wide. The donut, legend, rebalance rows and price chart use onMouseEnter/onMouseMove with no focus or touch path (0 onFocus handlers). Nav buttons lack aria-current.
findings.why: Fails WCAG 2.4.7 Focus Visible (AA) and 2.1.1 Keyboard (A). Double-click is unreliable on touch devices, so mobile users can't rename portfolios.
findings.fix: Remove outline:none, or use a token box-shadow focus ring. Add pencil and duplicate <IconButton aria-label="Renombrar portafolio X"> controls with targets of 40px or more. Mirror hover handlers with onFocus/onBlur and switch to pointer events for touch. Add `aria-current="page"` on the active nav item.

findings.title: Workspace has no headings, no <main> landmark, and no text alternatives for charts
findings.evidence: grep finds a single <h1> (LoginScreen, line 952) and no h2/h3; every section title is a styled div (e.g. 'COMPOSICIÓN DEL PORTAFOLIO', 2579). There is no <main>, even though theme.css:257 defines .app-main. The SVG charts have no role='img', aria-label or <title>. The 6 tables have no <caption> or scope.
findings.why: Screen-reader users can't navigate by headings or landmarks, and charts are announced as nothing (WCAG 1.1.1, 1.3.1, 2.4.1, 2.4.6).
findings.fix: Wrap content in <main className="app-main">. Render <PageHeader> (ui.jsx:57) with an h1 per tab and <SectionHeading> (h2) per panel. Give charts `role="img" aria-label="AAPL 1A: de US$X a US$Y (+Z%)"` plus an sr-only summary table. Add <caption> to data tables.

findings.title: Navigation IA: 8 flat tabs with Spanglish jargon, 4 divergent nav definitions, and no URL state
findings.evidence: Labels include 'Portfolio', 'Analytics vs SPY', 'Sharpe Optimizer', 'ML Screener', 'FIBRA Screener' and 'Fórmula Mágica'. The nav list is written 4 times with different labels and order: the sidebar starts with Portfolio while the default tab is 'news' and the bottom nav starts with Noticias. The breadcrumb 'Dashboard /' reflects no real hierarchy. The portfolio selector is re-implemented in 3 tabs with 3 styles. There is no pushState, hash or scroll reset.
findings.why: A Mexican retail user doesn't know what 'Sharpe Optimizer' or 'Analytics vs SPY' mean, and an MXN investor's natural benchmark is the IPC/NAFTRAC, not SPY. Reloading drops the user on Noticias. There are no deep links, and the back button leaves the app.
findings.fix: Use one `NAV` constant {id,label,short,icon,group}. Suggested IA: Mercados (Panorama, Noticias) · Mi portafolio (Posiciones, Rebalanceo, Riesgo y desempeño vs IPC y S&P en MXN, Optimizar pesos) · Empresa (Análisis) · Ideas (Screener cuantitativo, FIBRAs, Fórmula Mágica). Use hash routing (#/portafolio/rebalanceo), set document.title, and scroll to top on tab change. Move the portfolio switcher into the topbar as global context.

findings.title: Landing page repeats the same quotes 3-4 times while Mexico-specific data is missing; the whole app is blocked on backend cold start
findings.evidence: S&P, NASDAQ, DJIA, IPC and USD/MXN appear in the bento (3837-3845), again in Indicadores Principales (3887-3895), again as prose in the Resumen, and partly in the topbar strip. The bento alternates mint, dark and beige tiles (`bg: "#79df9b"`, `"#eceee8"`) purely for decoration. App renders only 'CONECTANDO AL SERVIDOR…' for up to 60s (AbortSignal.timeout(60000)) before even showing login. On failure it shows developer copy: 'Asegúrate de que Railway o Render estén activos, o corre python backend.py'.
findings.why: The repetition wastes the most valuable screen space, and the decorative color competes with the gain/loss colors. A 30-60s blank wait on Render's free tier with no explanation feels broken, and the error copy is meant for developers, not users.
findings.fix: Keep one index strip with sparklines and use the freed space for CETES, Bono M, TIIE, NAFTRAC, FIBRA index and the user's own portfolio day P&L. Render login and shell immediately with per-panel skeletons. Show 'Despertando el servidor (hasta 1 min)…' with progress. Error copy: 'No pudimos conectar con los datos de mercado. Reintentar'.

findings.title: Rebalance table overflows its card at common desktop widths; trades are not shown in MXN or in whole shares
findings.evidence: Row grid `"10px minmax(130px,1fr) 130px 95px 80px"` + 4×16px gap + 40px padding = 549px minimum. At 1440px each resp-grid-2 column is about 568px, minus 48px card padding and border ≈ 517px usable, so it overflows by about 30px. `.rebal-table-wrap { overflow-x:auto }` exists only inside the ≤768px media query. New shares are computed as `+(((tPct/100*base)/priceMXN_).toFixed(6))`.
findings.why: Content spills past the card border on laptops. Investors need the cash amount to trade, and BMV shares trade in whole units (US fractional shares depend on the broker).
findings.fix: Always apply overflow-x:auto, or stack the donut above the table below 1500px. Add a 'Monto a operar (MXN)' column. Round .MX targets to whole shares and show the leftover cash.

findings.title: Análisis header and chart are not usable on mobile or for analysis: overflow, no axes, hover-only
findings.evidence: The header is `display:flex, justifyContent:space-between` with no flexWrap, a 48px ticker ('CEMEXCPO.MX' is about 330px wide) and a 36px price. Period tabs have no wrap either. The chart SVG has no y-axis values, no dates, no volume and no previous-close line; the hovered value only appears via onMouseMove.
findings.why: At 390px the header overflows horizontally, which the global overflow-x hack hides by clipping. Without axes or dates the chart can't be read or cited. Touch users get no values at all.
findings.fix: Add flexWrap, and use font-size clamp(28px,8vw,48px) and clamp(24px,6vw,36px). Draw min/max/last price labels and start/end dates, and switch to onPointerMove/onPointerDown. Add an 'al cierre de <fecha>' label, 52-week range and volume bars.

findings.title: No reduced-motion support; infinite animations plus an auto-rotating login carousel with no pause
findings.evidence: grep finds no 'prefers-reduced-motion'. glowPulse loops forever on the LIVE badges and the status dot, stat-shimmer loops on headings, and the kaizen-mark floats. `setInterval(() => setQuoteIdx(...), 5000)` rotates quotes with no pause control. The same keyframes are redefined inside App.jsx's <style> (2067-2077).
findings.why: Violates WCAG 2.2.2 Pause, Stop, Hide (A). Constant motion distracts in a data-dense tool and causes discomfort for vestibular-sensitive users.
findings.fix: Add `@media (prefers-reduced-motion: reduce){*,*::before,*::after{animation:none!important;transition:none!important}html{scroll-behavior:auto}}`. Pause the carousel on hover/focus or show a static quote. Remove the duplicate keyframes from App.jsx.

findings.title: Design-system primitives exist but go unused; a global table override conflicts with tokens
findings.evidence: Usage counts in App.jsx: Card 0, KpiTile 0 (both imported on line 4 but unused), IconButton 0, PageHeader 0, SectionHeading 0, Metric 0, EmptyState 0, ProgressBar 0, .segmented-control 0, .data-table 0, and 737 inline style objects. There is a global `td { padding: 11px 14px; font-size: 14px }` in App.jsx. The segmented control is built four different ways: #/% toggle with bg-deep, optimizer periods with accent-strong, análisis periods with #135936, financials with #3b82f6.
findings.why: Every screen looks slightly different, theme fixes don't propagate, and a 5.5k-line component is hard to maintain or test.
findings.fix: Add SegmentedControl, PortfolioSwitcher, StatCard (built on Metric/KpiTile), DataTable (.data-table), ChangePill, Money and ChartFrame to ui.jsx. Remove the global table/th/td rules. Split App.jsx into /tabs/*.jsx with a shared formatters.js (fmtMoney, fmtPct, fmtCompact in the es-MX locale).

findings.title: Type is too small for dense financial data
findings.evidence: Inline font sizes: 1×8px, 3×8.5px, 49×9px, 86×10px. Examples: SectionLabel uses `fontSize: 9, letterSpacing: "0.2em"`; the MX macro period uses fontSize 8. In theme.css, .data-table thead is 0.58rem (about 9.3px) and .progress-label 0.56rem (about 9px).
findings.why: Uppercase, letter-spaced 8-9px labels are unreadable on phones and for older users. Terminal density comes from alignment and tabular layout, not from tiny text.
findings.fix: Add type tokens (--text-2xs 11px minimum for labels, --text-xs 12px, --text-sm 13px, --text-md 14px) and replace inline sizes. Keep JetBrains Mono for numbers and right-align numeric columns.

findings.title: Spanglish microcopy and inconsistent units
findings.evidence: Examples: 'Backend OK', 'P&L ($)', 'Sharpe · 1y' vs '1A' elsewhere, 'Income/Balance/Cash Flow', 'Revenue/Net Income', 'WTI Crude', 'safe-haven', 'risk-on'. Sentiment shows raw 'POSITIVE' in Análisis but 'Positiva' in Noticias. The spread appears as 'SPREAD 10Y +0.52' (topbar, no unit, and the 2Y leg unnamed), '+52 pb' (Resumen) and 'Spread +0.52' (Fear & Greed). 'Fear & Greed' is computed from VIX alone yet borrows CNN's composite-index name.
findings.why: Inconsistent terms and units make users doubt the numbers and read as unpolished to a Spanish-speaking audience.
findings.fix: Keep a glossary: Ganancia/Pérdida, Ingresos, Utilidad neta, Flujo de efectivo, 'Conectado', '1A'. Show the spread everywhere as 'Diferencial 10A–2A: +52 pb'. Rename the gauge to 'Termómetro de volatilidad (VIX)'.

findings.title: No onboarding: demo positions look like the user's own, and data lives only in localStorage with no export/import
findings.evidence: DEFAULT_PORTFOLIO seeds AAPL 10 @150, MSFT 8 @320, CEMEXCPO.MX 100 @8.5, etc. as 'Principal' with no 'ejemplo' label. savePortfolios writes only localStorage. The only download in the app is the EDGAR CSV.
findings.why: First-time users see fake P&L as their own and have to delete positions one by one. Clearing the browser or switching devices loses everything, which is a problem for the company-benefit use case.
findings.fix: First run: an <EmptyState> offering 'Agregar mi primera posición', 'Importar CSV (GBM/Actinver/IBKR)' and 'Ver portafolio de ejemplo' (demo clearly badged 'Ejemplo'). Add portfolio JSON/CSV export and import, then server-side persistence per user once real auth exists.

findings.title: Authentication is client-side only: the shared password ships in the JS bundle and every data endpoint is open with CORS *
findings.evidence: App.jsx:934 `if (pw === "Investments") { onAuth(); }`. The string is in the production build (dist/assets/index-BNl03Xe4.js contains ``t===`Investments`?e():``). The session is just `localStorage.setItem("kaizen_authed","1")` (58-60). The backend has check_login over a plaintext USERS env JSON (1845-1862) and POST /login returns `{"ok": True}` with no token (1953-1954), but nothing in src calls /login. do_GET (1878-1915) serves /stock, /chart, /fibras, /magic_one, /debug/macro etc. with no auth check. _cors sends `Access-Control-Allow-Origin: *` and `Allow-Headers: *` (1969-1972). /login has no attempt limit.
findings.why: Anyone who opens DevTools can read the password or set the localStorage flag, and anyone on the internet (any website, via CORS *) can use the Render backend as a free Yahoo proxy. You can't sell seats to companies with this: no per-user identity, no revocation, no audit trail, no protection against brute force (OWASP A01/A07). The backend USERS mechanism is dead code that suggests security exists when it doesn't.
findings.fix: Short term: delete the literal check. LoginScreen POSTs /login {username,password}. The backend verifies argon2/bcrypt hashes (not plaintext) and returns a signed token (PyJWT HS256 with SECRET_KEY env, exp 12 h). Every GET route requires `Authorization: Bearer`, returning 401 otherwise. Rate-limit /login to 5/min/IP. Replace CORS * with an ALLOWED_ORIGINS env allowlist (Vercel prod and preview domains, http://localhost:5173). Remove the localStorage flag and keep the token in memory plus sessionStorage. Target: Supabase Auth or Clerk with orgs/seats; FastAPI verifies the JWT via JWKS, and Postgres row-level security (RLS) protects user data.
findings.verify_reasoning:
I checked every factual claim against the code and could not refute any of them.

- **Password in the bundle.** src/App.jsx:934 has `if (pw === "Investments") { onAuth(); }`. The built file dist/assets/index-BNl03Xe4.js contains ``t===`Investments`?e():``, so the password ships to every visitor.
- **Session is a localStorage flag.** App.jsx:52-60 stores the "session" as `kaizen_authed = "1"` in localStorage. App.jsx:1039 gates the Workspace on that flag alone. Typing `localStorage.setItem('kaizen_authed','1')` in the console skips the login. VITE_SKIP_LOGIN is correctly limited to dev mode (line 53), so that path is fine.
- **Backend login is unused.** backend.py:1846-1862 checks plaintext passwords from the USERS env JSON. The comparison uses hmac.compare_digest, so it is constant-time; that part is fine. POST /login (1950-1956) only returns `{"ok": True}` and issues no token. Nothing in src calls /login: grep finds only lines 52 and 934. There are 23 raw fetch() calls in App.jsx and none send credentials.
- **Every GET route is open.** do_GET (1878-1915) serves stock, chart, rf, news, macro, market, worldmap, dcf, edgar, fibras, magic, magic_one, insiders, momentum, returns, fx, health and debug/macro with no auth check. Every response is HTTP 200, errors included.
- **CORS is fully open.** _cors (1969-1972) sends `Allow-Origin: *` and `Allow-Headers: *`.
- **No login rate limit.** /login has no attempt limit.

Two points soften the finding but do not refute it:
1. Only public market data sits behind the gate (Yahoo, FRED, SEC, RSS). Portfolios, the screener list and FIBRA data live in the user's own localStorage (App.jsx:801-814, 1105-1170). So no personal data leaks. The real harms are:
   - Anyone can use the Render service as a free proxy. That exhausts the free plan and invites Yahoo to rate-limit or ban its shared IP, which degrades the app for paying users.
   - /debug/macro makes 5 upstream calls per request, so it multiplies that abuse.
   - The app cannot offer per-seat access, revocation or audit, which the owner's plan to sell seats to companies requires.
   Under the rubric ("security hole" = critical), critical holds as a launch blocker. It is closer to high in terms of data exposure today.
2. The CORS allowlist only restricts JavaScript running on other websites. It does nothing against curl or scripts. Only authentication closes the proxy abuse. Brute-forcing /login is also pointless today, because /login gates nothing.

The proposed fix is right in direction but misses details that would break it if implemented literally:
- Per the Fetch spec, the `Access-Control-Allow-Headers: *` wildcard never covers `Authorization`. Once a Bearer token is added, the header must be listed explicitly, or browsers will fail the preflight.
- OPTIONS and /health must stay unauthenticated. detectBackend (App.jsx:37-45) probes /health before the login screen appears.
- do_GET hard-codes send_response(200), so returning 401 needs a restructure.
- Behind Render's proxy, the client IP for rate limiting has to come from X-Forwarded-For.
- Any secret passed through a VITE_ env variable is still embedded in the bundle, so that is not a fix either.
- The 23 fetch calls need one shared wrapper.
- Supabase RLS is premature, because no user data is stored on the server yet.
findings.corrected_fix:
Backend (backend.py):
1. Store bcrypt or argon2 hashes in the USERS env JSON instead of plaintext, for example `{"arturo":"$argon2id$..."}`. Verify with argon2-cffi or bcrypt. Keep the constant-time comparison.
2. POST /login returns `{"token": jwt}` on success. Sign it with PyJWT HS256 using a SECRET_KEY env var, with claims sub=username, exp=now+12h, iat. Return HTTP 401 on bad credentials.
3. Rate-limit /login to about 5 attempts per minute per IP. Take the IP from the first entry of X-Forwarded-For (Render sits behind a proxy); an in-memory dict with a lock is enough for a single ThreadingHTTPServer instance.
4. In do_GET, before routing: if parts[0] is not "health", require `Authorization: Bearer <jwt>` and verify it with jwt.decode(..., algorithms=["HS256"]). On failure, send_response(401) with `{"error":"auth"}`. This means replacing the hard-coded send_response(200) with a status variable.
5. Leave OPTIONS unauthenticated.
6. Delete /debug/macro, or put it behind an ADMIN user. Stop returning str(e) to clients: log the detail and return a generic message.
7. In _cors, echo the Origin only if it is in an ALLOWED_ORIGINS env allowlist (the Vercel production domain, the project's preview pattern, http://localhost:5173) and add `Vary: Origin`. Set `Access-Control-Allow-Headers: Authorization, Content-Type` explicitly, because `*` does not cover Authorization. Keep `Allow-Methods: GET, POST, OPTIONS`.

Frontend (src/App.jsx):
1. Delete the literal check at line 934. LoginScreen gets a username field and POSTs `${BACKEND}/login`. On success, keep the token in a module-level variable mirrored to sessionStorage. Remove AUTH_KEY, readAuthed and writeAuthed (lines 52-60), and the localStorage flag.
2. Add one `apiFetch(path, opts)` wrapper that attaches `Authorization: Bearer`. On a 401 it clears the token and calls onLogout. Route all 23 fetch() calls through it; detectBackend's /health probe is the one exception.
3. Never put a secret in a VITE_ env variable, because those are embedded in the bundle.
4. Rebuild so dist/ no longer contains the password, and rotate "Investments" if it was reused anywhere.

Target, when seats are sold: Supabase Auth or Clerk with organisations and seats. The backend verifies the provider's JWT through JWKS, with per-user rate limits and audit logs. Row-level security only becomes relevant once portfolios move to the server; today they live in each user's localStorage.

findings.title: Expensive per-ticker endpoints are uncached and unthrottled, so one user or bot can get the shared Render IP rate-limited by Yahoo
findings.evidence: _cached is used only for macro (626), market (704), worldmap (725), edgar (1175), magic (1337), fx_hist (498) and rf (1820-1835). get_stock (179) calls `t.info` fresh every time with `time.sleep(2)` retries (192). get_chart, get_dcf, get_magic_one, get_news, get_market_news (6 yfinance news calls plus up to 9 RSS feeds), get_fx, get_insiders, get_momentum and get_returns have no cache. get_fibras loops sequentially `for ticker in tickers:` (1488) over 10 FIBRAs plus up to `_FIBRAS_EXTRA_MAX = 20` extras, each doing .info + fast_info + _fetch_hist (1.5 s retry sleep), all uncached. Public /debug/macro (1907-1914) triggers FRED×2, CBOE, Stooq and a yf bulk download on every hit. There is no per-IP or per-user limit, and every request gets a new thread (1994-1997).
findings.why: Yahoo throttles by source IP. On Render all users share one egress IP, so one heavy session, or any scraper given CORS * and no auth, exhausts the quota and everyone gets empty prices. Without a cache, every reload re-pays 1–3 s of .info latency. A single /fibras/<20 tickers> call can hold a thread for 1–2 minutes.
findings.fix: Wrap each per-ticker function with _cached, with TTLs by data class: quote 60 s during market hours and 15 min when closed; info/fundamentals 12–24 h (split quote from fundamentals so a price refresh doesn't re-pull .info); daily chart 1 h, weekly 6 h; dcf 12 h; news and market_news 10 min; fx 60 s with last-good fallback; fibras 30 min keyed by the sorted extra list. Use ok= predicates so failures are cached only 30–60 s. Add a token-bucket limiter per user/IP (slowapi once on FastAPI) with tighter buckets for /fibras/* and /magic_one. Delete /debug/* or gate it behind an ADMIN_TOKEN header. Later, move the cache to Redis (Render Key Value or Upstash) so it survives restarts and cold starts.
findings.verify_reasoning:
I checked every claim against backend.py and the callers in src/App.jsx. They hold up.

Cache coverage
- `_cached` (backend.py:69-92, single-flight, 500-entry cap) is used only at these call sites: macro 626, market 704, worldmap 725, edgar 1175, magic 1337 and fx_hist 498. rf uses `_cache_get`/`_cache_put` by hand (1820-1835).
- None of these call any cache: get_stock 179, get_fx 441, get_returns 453, get_chart 479 (only its FX series is cached), get_market_news 756, get_dcf 806 (`t.info` at about 844, plus an uncached FX `history` at about 873), get_magic_one 1341, get_fibras 1466, get_insiders 1650, get_momentum 1708, get_news 1801.

Per-endpoint cost
- **get_stock:** loops on `t.info` with `time.sleep(2)` (184-192). If both attempts fail it sleeps 4 s, because the sleep also runs after the last attempt. It then always pulls `t.financials`, `income_stmt`, `balance_sheet` and `cashflow` (231-269), and when beta or the 52w change is missing it adds `_fetch_hist(ticker)` and `_fetch_hist("SPY")` (351-383). One /stock call is roughly 5-8 Yahoo requests.
- **get_market_news:** 6 `.news` calls (761-773), plus up to 9 RSS feeds when fewer than 5 items come back (776-800).
- **get_fibras:** runs strictly one ticker after another (`for ticker in tickers:` at 1488) over 10 base names plus up to `_FIBRAS_EXTRA_MAX = 20` extras (1484, 1867). One detail in the finding is wrong, and it understates the load: `fast_info` and `_fetch_hist` only run as fallbacks (1503-1512, 1528). But `balance_sheet`, `cashflow` and `income_stmt` run for every ticker (1541, 1557, 1563), plus an FX `history` call whenever currencies differ (1593). So each FIBRA costs about 4-6 requests, in series, and 1-2 minutes for 30 tickers is plausible.
- **/debug/macro (1907-1914):** public. It calls `_fred_rate` twice, `_cboe_vix`, `_stooq_dxy` and `_bulk_download` directly on every request, skipping the macro cache.

Server exposure
- `ThreadingHTTPServer` with `daemon_threads` and `request_queue_size = 128` (1994-1997) opens a new thread per request.
- `_cors` sends `Allow-Origin: *` (1970).
- There is no rate limiting anywhere, and GET endpoints need no auth. Login exists only as a localStorage flag on the client (App.jsx:56-59).
- render.yaml runs `plan: free` with `python backend.py`. The in-memory cache is lost whenever the instance spins down, and outbound traffic uses Render's shared regional egress IPs.

The frontend makes it worse (the finding misses this)
1. **Magic Formula button:** `runMagicFormula` (App.jsx:1766-1782) calls `/magic_one` one by one for a 128-ticker `MAGIC_UNIVERSE`. Each call is uncached and does `.info`, `income_stmt` and `balance_sheet`, so about 380 Yahoo requests per click. Meanwhile the backend already has a `/magic` endpoint that is cached for 12 h and prewarmed at startup (1334-1338, 1978-1985), and the UI never calls it.
2. **/fx used as a health probe:** the keep-alive pings /fx every 9 min per open tab (App.jsx:1242-1249), and `ensureBackend` polls /fx every 6 s for up to 2 min (1440-1451). Every probe is an uncached `USDMXN=X` history call.
3. **Duplicate work on retries:** `fetchStock` gives up after 30 s and retries 3 times (App.jsx:105-121), but the server thread for the abandoned request keeps running.
4. **Screener:** for each ticker it calls /stock, /chart, /dcf and /momentum (App.jsx:1715-1740). That is 3 separate `.info` pulls for the same ticker, and momentum re-downloads the sector ETF (for example XLK) every time (1720-1721).

Severity and fix
High severity is justified. With no cache, even one normal user can push hundreds of Yahoo requests from the shared Render egress IP, and when Yahoo returns 429 every user's prices go blank.

The proposed fix is right in direction but has two gaps:
- slowapi does not apply, because this is stdlib `http.server`, not FastAPI. A limiter has to live in `Handler.do_GET`. Behind Render's proxy, `self.client_address` is the proxy, so the client IP must come from the first entry of `X-Forwarded-For`.
- `_cached` does not cache exceptions, and get_chart and get_fx can raise or fall back. Failures need to be turned into error results so the `fail_ttl` negative cache actually works. Otherwise a bot sending invalid tickers hits Yahoo on every request.

A minor point on TTLs: Yahoo's BMV quotes are already delayed about 15-20 min, so a 60 s quote TTL buys nothing for .MX tickers.
