- /magic_one (:1341).
- /insiders (:1650): NOT used by the frontend, although README line 46 lists 'Insiders' as a feature.
- /momentum (:1708), /returns (:453), /fx (:441, falls back to 17.5), /health.
- /debug/macro (:1907): public.
- POST /login (:1950): checks a USERS env var but is NEVER called by the frontend.

No GET endpoint requires authentication, and CORS is '*' (:1969-1972). There is a TTL cache (:43-93) and ticker-format validation (:1866-1885). Nearly all data comes from yfinance through yft() (:31).
strengths: Portfolio analytics are measured in pesos: /chart?ccy=MXN converts USD prices with the USD/MXN rate of the same date (backend.py:479-513). Sharpe, the optimizer, the backtest and Monte Carlo therefore run in MXN against a Mexican risk-free rate (App.jsx:127-147). This is the right framing for Mexican investors and rare in retail tools.

Fallbacks say they are fallbacks. get_rf labels its fixed value 'ref. fija' (backend.py:1840-1841), get_fx returns fallback:true (:450), and fetchRiskFreeRate returns ok:false so the UI does not show 'Backend OK' on a hard-coded number (App.jsx:156-158). This culture of data honesty is worth extending to every quote.

The FIBRA screener is a real differentiator for Mexico, with REIT-style metrics: cap rate, P/NAV, LTV, distribution yield, and user-added tickers (backend.py:1458-1647, App.jsx:4550-4710). US-centric tools (Koyfin, Finviz) do not cover FIBRAs well.

Official US financials come straight from SEC EDGAR XBRL, with a compliant User-Agent and a CSV download (backend.py:1044-1177, App.jsx:85-103, 5394-5459). This is a free, license-clean primary source.
Solid portfolio-construction core: multiple portfolios, a cash line, allocation by shares or %, and a rebalance table with target sliders and share deltas in MXN (App.jsx:2302-2507, 2690-2980).

The benchmark analytics have the right textbook set (beta, tracking error, Treynor, Jensen alpha, information ratio) plus a glossary (App.jsx:249-307, 4422-4441). Monte Carlo draws correlated shocks, so the probability of beating SPY is not inflated (App.jsx:1654-1668).

The magic-formula universe excludes financials, utilities and REITs, as Greenblatt specifies (backend.py:1040-1043; App.jsx:1762-1764). Momentum is measured relative to the sector ETF, not in absolute terms (backend.py:124-131, 1708).

Backend hygiene is better than typical prototypes: a TTL cache with a separate short TTL for failures (backend.py:43-93), ticker regex validation (:1866-1885), a POST body cap (:1868, 1934), a threaded server with a 128-connection queue (:1994-1997), and FRED as the primary rates source with CBOE, Stooq and Yahoo fallbacks (:569-622).

The market overview is already broad: US, Mexican and global indices, FX crosses, commodities, crypto, a style box, and country ETFs (App.jsx:3834-4132). The Bloomberg-lite breadth is there; what is missing is depth and correctness.

Mexico-aware details already exist: tickers ending in .MX are treated as MXN (App.jsx:15-24), USD/MXN is shown in the rebalance header (App.jsx:2696), and the UI is in Spanish with a light/dark theme that follows the system (src/theme.js).

gaps.feature: P0 - Real authentication and per-user accounts to replace the shared client-side password (severity: critical, security)
gaps.why_valuable: The password check `if (pw === "Investments")` sits in client code at App.jsx:934 and ships in the production bundle: dist/assets/index-BNl03Xe4.js contains t===`Investments`. The session is only localStorage 'kaizen_authed'='1' (App.jsx:52-60), which anyone can set in devtools. Backend POST /login with a USERS env var (backend.py:1845-1862, 1950) is never called. Every GET endpoint is open with CORS '*' (backend.py:1878-1915, 1969-1972), and /debug/macro is public (:1907). Anyone can use the Render backend as a free Yahoo proxy, which invites rate-limit bans that hit all users. Accounts are also the prerequisite for paid tiers, employer seats and server-side portfolios. Fix: managed OIDC auth (Supabase Auth, Clerk or Auth0); verify a short-lived JWT on every backend route; add per-user and per-IP rate limits; restrict CORS to the Vercel origin; remove /debug.
gaps.data_source: N/A (managed auth provider: Supabase Auth / Clerk / Auth0; Postgres for users)

gaps.feature: P0 - Remove the fabricated quarterly financials on the Análisis page (severity: critical, wrong numbers)
gaps.why_valuable: App.jsx:5019-5023 invents Q1-Q4 figures: `quarters = annual => { base = annual/4; return [base*0.88, base*0.96, base*1.05, base*1.11] }`. Revenue, net income, operating cash flow and free cash flow always show a fake rising trend. It also splits balance-sheet stocks (total assets, total debt) into 'quarters' (:5032-5036), which is meaningless. The only caveat is '* anual estimado por trimestres' in #374151 on a near-black panel (:5364), practically invisible. Users will read made-up growth. Fix now: show the annual values only. Next: real quarterly data from SEC EDGAR 10-Q facts for US names (the backend already parses companyfacts at backend.py:1089-1177), and a licensed fundamentals feed for BMV names; yfinance quarterly_income_stmt only as a personal-beta stopgap.
gaps.data_source: SEC EDGAR XBRL companyfacts (free) for US; licensed fundamentals (EODHD/FMP) for .MX; yfinance quarterly statements only as a non-commercial stopgap

gaps.feature: P0 - Transaction ledger with FX-correct cost basis, realized vs unrealized P&L, dividends, fees, and TWR plus MWR/XIRR performance (severity: critical, wrong P&L)
gaps.why_valuable: Holdings are a snapshot {ticker, shares, cost} with no dates (App.jsx:62-68). posCostMXN converts USD cost at TODAY's USD/MXN (App.jsx:22-24, `priceMXN(p.ticker, p.cost ?? 0, usdMxn)`), so the MXN P&L of US stocks leaves out the currency gain or loss. Example: AAPL bought at $150 when USD/MXN was 20 (3,000 MXN) and now at $200 with USD/MXN at 17.5 (3,500 MXN) is +16.7% in pesos, but the app shows +33.3%. 'Aplicar rebalanceo' overwrites shares and keeps the old average cost (App.jsx:2924-2934, `{ ...x, shares: newShares }`), which inflates P&L after buys and never records realized gains on sells. 'Eliminar' deletes a position with no confirmation and no realized P&L record (App.jsx:3170). With no dates there is no annualized return. You also cannot compute TWR (the GIPS measure of skill, independent of cash flows) or MWR/XIRR (what the investor actually earned), and every serious tool shows both. Fix: a lots/transactions table (buy, sell, dividend, split, fee, deposit, withdrawal, fx_rate_at_trade, tax_withheld); average cost per Mexican practice; a daily valuation series; TWR by daily linking (or Modified Dietz); XIRR; realized/unrealized split in MXN and in the original currency.
gaps.data_source: User input or broker import; historical USD/MXN from Banxico SIE FIX SF43718 (free); price history from the market-data vendor

gaps.feature: P0 - Compliance layer: disclaimers and no personalized buy/sell verbs (severity: high, regulatory)
gaps.why_valuable: There is no disclaimer anywhere: grep for asesor|disclaimer|no constituye|CNBV returns 0 hits. The app labels stocks BUY/HOLD/SELL (App.jsx:378, shown at :3543-3565). It shows 'RECOMENDACIONES PARA TU PORTAFOLIO' with AGREGAR/CONSIDERAR/OMITIR computed from the user's own holdings (App.jsx:3436-3458), and flags FIBRAs as 'OPORTUNIDAD' (backend.py:1623). Personalized recommendations can be read as 'asesoría de inversiones', which in Mexico requires CNBV registration as an asesor en inversiones (LMV arts. 225-227; confirm with Mexican securities counsel). An employer distributing the tool takes on that exposure too. Fix: a persistent footer plus a first-run acknowledgment ('Información con fines educativos; no constituye recomendación ni asesoría de inversión'). Replace verbs with transparent rule checklists such as 'cumple 5/8 criterios' (port Kaizen02 src/lib/policy.ts pass/watch/fail). Add a methodology page per score and a risk disclosure page.
gaps.data_source: N/A (legal copy reviewed by Mexican counsel)

gaps.feature: P0 - Live Mexican macro and rates from Banxico SIE and INEGI, and CETES 28 as the risk-free rate (severity: high)
gaps.why_valuable: The 'México · Macro' panel is a hard-coded array (App.jsx:3729-3737: INPC 4.53%, TIIE 28D 7.02%, 'Banxico May 2026', reserves '24 Abr 2026'), displayed as data (:4072-4094) on a page with pulsing LIVE badges. As of September 2026 it is about four months stale. The risk-free rate behind every Sharpe is the 10Y Bono M from a monthly OECD series on FRED (backend.py:1814-1841). It lags one to two months and carries a long-duration term premium; Sharpe on weekly returns should subtract a short rate (CETES 28 days), otherwise every Sharpe is biased down. The top bar shows only US macro (App.jsx:2237-2255). Fix: Banxico SIE with a free token. Use FIX SF43718, target rate SF61745 and annual INPC SP30578, which already appear in Kaizen02 Material/dashboard-arauco/build_snapshot.py:123-125. Add CETES 28/91/182/364 auction yields, TIIE and UDI (check the series IDs in the SIE catalog). From INEGI's BIE API (free token): PIB, IGAE, ENOE unemployment, INPC quincenal. Add a Mexico strip to the top bar: USD/MXN FIX, Banxico target, CETES 28, INPC y/y, IPC.
gaps.data_source: Banxico SIE API (free token), INEGI BIE API (free token)

gaps.feature: P0 (before charging anyone) - Licensed market-data provider behind a provider interface, retiring yfinance for commercial use
gaps.why_valuable: Almost every endpoint goes through yft(), i.e. yfinance (backend.py:31, 179, 441, 479, 1466, 1650). yfinance scrapes Yahoo's unofficial endpoints; its documentation points to Yahoo's terms (personal use), and Yahoo does not allow commercial redistribution. Yahoo also rate-limits cloud IPs more and more, and the code already fights this with retries and sleeps (App.jsx:105-121, 129-147; backend.py:183-193). A paid product or employer benefit built on this is both a legal and an uptime risk. Fix: a provider abstraction (pattern: Kaizen02 src/services/marketData.ts plus its docs/DATA-PROVIDERS.md activation checklist); store the source and as-of time for every value; sign a vendor contract with written rights for commercial display and caching (see data_licensing).
gaps.data_source: Licensed vendor (EODHD / Financial Modeling Prep / Twelve Data) plus free official sources

gaps.feature: P0 - Honest data freshness: as-of timestamps, delay labels, remove the fake 'LIVE' badges and '+0.00' changes
gaps.why_valuable: Pulsing 'LIVE' badges (App.jsx:708, 977) and 'Datos en vivo' (App.jsx:985, index.html:11) appear while Yahoo BMV quotes are delayed and the Mexican macro table is static. The backend hard-codes "change": 0 for FRED, CBOE and Stooq values (backend.py:573, 583, 585), so the top bar always shows a green '+0.00' next to VIX, DXY and 10Y (App.jsx:2248), implying no movement. No quote carries a timestamp; only /rf returns asOf (backend.py:1834). Fix: return asOf, delayMinutes and source with every quote. Label the UI like 'BMV · retraso 20 min · 14:32'. Compute real day changes from the previous close, or hide them. Show a banner when the fallback flags are set (get_fx :450, get_rf :1841).
gaps.data_source: Existing sources, plus vendor timestamps once licensed

gaps.feature: P0 - Server-side encrypted persistence and multi-device sync
gaps.why_valuable: Portfolios, screener lists and the FIBRA cache live only in localStorage (App.jsx:799-815, 1105, 1130, 1808). Clearing the browser loses them, and there is no phone/desktop sync and no backup. Accounts, seats, alerts that run while the user is offline, and ARCO data requests are all impossible without a server store. Fix: Postgres (Supabase or Neon) with row-level security per user, encryption at rest, export and delete endpoints, and a one-time migration of existing localStorage data.
gaps.data_source: N/A (Postgres / Supabase)

gaps.feature: P1 - Command palette (Cmd/Ctrl+K) with ticker autocomplete and URL-addressable views (the Bloomberg keyboard workflow)
gaps.why_valuable: Tabs are useState (App.jsx:1046), so there are no deep links, no back button and no shareable ticker page. The Análisis search is a bare input with no suggestions and requires the exact Yahoo suffix (App.jsx:5121-5133, placeholder 'CEMEXCPO.MX'). Typing 'bimbo' should resolve to BIMBOA.MX. A keyboard-first flow ('WALMEX Enter', '/' to search, g+p for portfolio) is the core of the 'terminal' promise. Fix: react-router routes (/t/:symbol, /portafolio/:id, /mercados, and so on). Port Kaizen02 src/components/GlobalSearch.tsx, which already has the Cmd+K dialog, focus trap, inert background and Escape handling. Build a symbol master from SEC company_tickers.json (already fetched at backend.py:1057-1070) plus a curated BMV/SIC catalog with Spanish names and aliases.
gaps.data_source: SEC company_tickers.json (free); BMV/SIC issuer list (curated static JSON now, vendor symbol list later)

gaps.feature: P1 - Watchlists with alerts and notifications
gaps.why_valuable: There is no watchlist or alert code (grep: 0 hits); the only way to track a symbol is to put it in the portfolio. Alerts are the daily-habit loop: price, % move, 52-week high/low, P/E band, ex-dividend date, FIBRA yield, CETES auction rate. Fix: a watchlist model; a backend scheduler that evaluates rules on cached quotes; notifications by email (Resend/SES), web push (PWA), and optionally WhatsApp (paid Meta/Twilio). Starting points: the Kaizen02 AlertRule type (src/types.ts:148-156), Watchlist type (:111-115) and AlertsPage UI (src/pages/app/UtilityPages.tsx:11-24).
gaps.data_source: Existing quote feed plus email/web-push infrastructure

gaps.feature: P1 - Mexican fixed-income module: CETES, Bonos M, Udibonos, UDI, yield curve
gaps.why_valuable: There is no CETES or government-bond content anywhere (grep: 0 hits). Yet CETES (via cetesdirecto) are the default first investment for Mexican retail savers and the hurdle every stock should beat. Show: latest weekly auction yields by tenor; real rate (CETES minus expected inflation from Banxico's survey of expectations); nominal and real yield curves; UDI value and Udibono real yields; a 'CETES vs this stock or portfolio' comparison after ISR withholding; a reinvestment simulator.
gaps.data_source: Banxico SIE (auction results, UDI, survey of expectations; free). Secondary-market Bono M/Udibono prices need Valmer or PiP (licensed).

gaps.feature: P1 - Mexican tax engine and tax/fee-aware rebalancing (ISR 10% on BMV/SIC gains, dividend withholding, FIBRA distributions, CETES interest)
gaps.why_valuable: Rebalance deltas (App.jsx:2896-2907) ignore broker commissions (about 0.1-0.25% plus IVA at Mexican brokers), bid-ask spread and ISR, and all P&L is pre-tax. Mexican individuals pay 10% ISR on the net annual gain from BMV/SIC shares, with cost updated by INPC (LISR art. 129). There is an extra 10% withholding on dividends paid from post-2014 CUFIN (art. 140) and 10% US treaty withholding on SIC US dividends. FIBRA distributions of fiscal result are withheld (30%), while reembolsos de capital are not. CETES interest has an annual withholding rate on capital set each year in the LIF. Fix: after-tax returns; estimated ISR and fees before 'Aplicar rebalanceo'; an annual gains/losses and dividends summary to reconcile against the broker's constancia. Have a contador validate the rules.
gaps.data_source: INPC from INEGI/Banxico (free) plus the transaction ledger; broker fee schedules (manual)

gaps.feature: P1 - Risk dashboard: max drawdown, VaR/CVaR, Sortino, USD/MXN exposure, sector/country concentration, effective N, selectable benchmark
gaps.why_valuable: Risk today means volatility, Sharpe and beta vs SPY (App.jsx:1533-1541). The benchmark is hard-wired to SPY in both the backtest and Monte Carlo (App.jsx:1474, 1593), which is the wrong yardstick for a peso investor; offer S&P/BMV IPC (^MXX), CETES, a 60/40 in MXN, or ACWI in MXN. Missing: max drawdown and recovery time, historical VaR and CVaR at 95%, Sortino, and the share of the portfolio in USD vs MXN (the largest single risk factor for Mexicans). Also missing: sector and country weights, HHI and effective number of positions (1/HHI), and position-limit breaches. The backtest applies today's weights to the past 5 years (App.jsx:1490-1504) and should be labeled 'simulación hipotética con pesos actuales' because of hindsight and survivorship bias.
gaps.data_source: Existing price history; sector/country from the fundamentals vendor; ^MXX and CETES series

gaps.feature: P1 - Dividend and FIBRA distribution calendar with income projection
gaps.why_valuable: The backend already returns dividendYield (backend.py:421), but the portfolio never displays it, and there are no ex-dates, payment dates or history. Recurring MXN income from FIBRAs and BMV dividends, net of withholding, is a primary goal for Mexican retail investors and a strong reason to come back to the app.
gaps.data_source: yfinance dividends (personal-beta stopgap only); EODHD/FMP dividends API (licensed); BMV 'avisos de derechos' / Indeval corporate actions (licensing unclear)

gaps.feature: P1 - Economic calendar for Mexico and the US
gaps.why_valuable: There is no calendar (grep: 0 hits). Banxico decisions (8 per year), INEGI releases (INPC quincenal, PIB oportuno, IGAE, employment), FOMC meetings and BLS CPI/NFP drive the peso, rates and the IPC. Show date/time, previous and actual values, and impact on the user's holdings. Consensus forecasts need a licensed feed.
gaps.data_source: INEGI 'calendario de difusión', Banxico publication calendar, FRED releases/dates API, BLS release schedule (all free). Consensus via Trading Economics or Econoday (licensed; pricing uncertain).

gaps.feature: P1 - Earnings calendar and results (estimate, actual, surprise) for holdings and watchlist
gaps.why_valuable: There are no earnings dates, estimates or surprises, although the next report is the most important catalyst for a stockholder. A 'Mi semana' view (earnings, dividends and macro events that touch my holdings) is a Bloomberg-like habit feature.
gaps.data_source: FMP / Finnhub / EODHD earnings calendars (licensed); SEC EDGAR 8-K/10-Q for US actuals (free); BMV quarterly reports via EMISNET (reuse terms uncertain)

gaps.feature: P1 - Broker import (GBM, Bursanet, Actinver, Kuspit, IBKR) plus CSV/PDF reports
gaps.why_valuable: Positions are entered one at a time, with no dates (App.jsx:2394-2507). That is the biggest onboarding blocker for real users and makes the ledger impractical. Start with a generic CSV template and column mapper, then add per-broker parsers for movement exports and account statements. Check which brokers offer CSV and which only PDF; PDF parsing is costlier. Add a monthly PDF/CSV report covering holdings, TWR/MWR, dividends and estimated ISR. The only export today is the EDGAR CSV (App.jsx:85-103).
gaps.data_source: User-uploaded broker files

gaps.feature: P1 - Education layer: tooltip on every metric, glossary and short learning paths in Spanish
gaps.why_valuable: The app shows dozens of metrics (P/E, PEG, PEGY, EV/EBITDA, P/B, ROE, cap rate, P/NAV, LTV, Treynor, Jensen, tracking error, information ratio). There is one static glossary, only in Analytics (App.jsx:4422-4441). Thresholds such as Sharpe '≥1.0 excelente' (App.jsx:2659, 3594) have no context about period, asset class or estimation error. For an employer wellness program, education is the product. Fix: a reusable <Term> tooltip with definition, formula, 'cómo leerlo', caveats and source; a linked glossary page; 5-minute lessons on compound interest, CETES, diversification, currency risk, fees and taxes.
gaps.data_source: In-house content (CONDUSEF/CONSAR public materials as references)

gaps.feature: P1 - Goals and retirement planner (AFORE, voluntary contributions, PPR) in real, inflation-adjusted MXN
gaps.why_valuable: The current Monte Carlo covers 52 weeks in nominal terms vs SPY (App.jsx:1651). There is nothing on goals, inflation or retirement, which is the core of employer financial wellness. Include: AFORE balance projection using CONSAR net-return data by SIEFORE generacional; voluntary contributions; deductibility of PPR and voluntary contributions (LISR art. 151-V: up to 10% of income, capped at 5 annual UMA; confirm the current UMA); real projections with the probability of reaching each goal; emergency-fund and education goals.
gaps.data_source: CONSAR open data (free), Banxico inflation-expectations survey (free), UMA from INEGI (free)

gaps.feature: P1 - Investor risk-profile questionnaire (perfil de inversionista)
gaps.why_valuable: There is no user profile. Defaults such as the fixed 35-ticker candidate list (App.jsx:71-79) and the 2-35% weight bounds (App.jsx:203-204) ignore horizon and risk tolerance. A short questionnaire can set the educational framing, the default benchmark and allocation guardrails without crossing into advice. Kaizen02's onboarding (src/pages/auth/AuthPages.tsx:56-62: goal, markets, asset classes) is a base to extend.
gaps.data_source: N/A

gaps.feature: P1 - Fix misleading labels: 'ML Screener', 'Fear & Greed', Resumen mood, news sentiment and attribution
gaps.why_valuable:
- The scorer calls itself rule-based in code ('Rule-Based Quantitative Engine', App.jsx:309) but is branded 'ML Screener' (App.jsx:2177, README).
- The screener copy promises 6 dimensions but lists 5 plus Overall (App.jsx:3533-3535).
- Momentum and Technical both score on priceChange52w, so the same signal is counted twice (App.jsx:337-367).
- 'Fear & Greed' is just 100 minus a linear VIX transform (App.jsx:3987), not a multi-factor index.
- The Resumen counts 'warning' items (VIX 20-30 'cautela', oil up 'presión inflacionaria') as positive (App.jsx:687).
- News sentiment uses substring matching (backend.py:1778-1784): 'gain' matches 'against', 'revenue' counts as positive, 'debt' as negative.
- Every RSS item is credited to 'Yahoo Finance', even CNBC and MarketWatch stories (backend.py:752).

Fix: rename to 'Score Kaizen (reglas)' and 'Termómetro VIX'; score each signal once; exclude warnings from the positive count; use exact-token or model-based sentiment, or drop the badges; credit the real publisher.
gaps.data_source: N/A

gaps.feature: P1 - FIBRA screener metric integrity (real FFO/AFFO, NAV, occupancy, distribution history)
gaps.why_valuable: 'FFO Yield' is actually free cash flow over market cap (backend.py:1473, 1584-1607) and falls back to operating cash flow (:1559). The UI even describes it as 'Free Cash Flow / Market Cap' (App.jsx:4598). FFO per NAREIT/AMEFIBRA is net income plus real-estate D&A minus gains on property sales, adjusted for fair-value and FX effects. P/NAV is Yahoo's priceToBook (backend.py:1521). The 'OPORTUNIDAD' signal uses P/NAV < 0.85 alone (:1623), ignoring LTV, occupancy and distribution coverage. Yahoo's dividend yield often misses reembolsos de capital. Fix: take FFO/AFFO, NAV, occupancy and distributions from FIBRA quarterly reports (AMEFIBRA standardized FFO); show distribution history and its tax character.
gaps.data_source: FIBRA quarterly reports / EMISNET (manual curation) or a licensed fundamentals vendor

gaps.feature: P1 - Mexico-first screeners and a fast Fórmula Mágica using the existing backend cache
gaps.why_valuable: The Fórmula Mágica covers about 140 US names only, yet the header says 'S&P 500' (App.jsx:4723). It runs about 140 sequential browser requests with 80 ms sleeps (App.jsx:1766-1798), and its universe includes the invalid tickers 'PALO' (App.jsx:1750; should be PANW) and 'SBKS' (App.jsx:1753; should be SBUX). Meanwhile the backend already computes this ranking, caches it for 12h and prewarms it (backend.py:1334-1338, 1978-1985), and nothing calls it. There is no BMV screener beyond 14 default tickers (App.jsx:70). Fix: call /magic; add BMV/SIC universes (IPC constituents, FIBRAs, SIC ETFs); saved screens; a sortable table view; CSV export.
gaps.data_source: Licensed fundamentals for .MX (yfinance coverage of BMV fundamentals is patchy)

gaps.feature: P1 - Performance and reliability: paid backend, batch endpoints, nightly precompute
gaps.why_valuable: The Render free plan (render.yaml `plan: free`) sleeps when idle. First load waits up to 60 s per backend candidate (App.jsx:40), then shows 'Despertando backend… hasta 90 s' (App.jsx:1464-1466) inside a 120 s wait loop (App.jsx:1442). Every open tab pings /fx every 9 minutes to keep the server awake (App.jsx:1240-1248). The optimizer, screener and backtest fetch tickers one by one from the browser (App.jsx:1330-1340, 1484-1488, 1709-1743). Fix: a paid instance plus a Redis cache; /batch endpoints; scheduled jobs for screeners, macro and FIBRAs; skeleton loading states.
gaps.data_source: N/A (infrastructure)

gaps.feature: P1 - Automated tests for the financial math, plus CI
gaps.why_valuable: The repo has no test files. Code comments show the money math has already regressed several times: covariance windows (App.jsx:192), infeasible weight bounds (:208), uncorrelated Monte Carlo draws (:1654-1655), a stale Sharpe cache key (:1862-1864). A paid product needs unit tests for Sharpe, covariance, P&L, FX conversion, TWR/XIRR and tax rules. Port Kaizen02's Vitest + Playwright + axe setup and its gates (CLAUDE.md: two viewports, WCAG AA).
gaps.data_source: N/A

gaps.feature: P1 - Currency clarity and safer destructive actions
gaps.why_valuable: Position cards print '$' for USD prices, cost and P&L (App.jsx:3027, 3046-3049) next to MXN totals (App.jsx:2731-2737) with no currency code. 'Eliminar' deletes instantly (App.jsx:3170). New users see a demo portfolio with invented costs (App.jsx:62-68) presented as if it were theirs. Fix: always show the ISO currency code and an MXN equivalent; confirm or undo on delete; label the demo as 'Portafolio de ejemplo' and add an empty-state onboarding that offers import.
gaps.data_source: N/A

gaps.feature: P1 (employer channel) - Employer admin console, SSO, seats, invoicing (CFDI 4.0)
gaps.why_valuable: The app currently has a single shared password (App.jsx:934) and no concept of a user or organization, so it cannot be sold to employers. Minimum set: org tenants; SSO via SAML/OIDC (Microsoft Entra ID, Google Workspace); SCIM or CSV seat provisioning; admin roles that cannot see holdings; aggregated anonymized engagement reports; per-seat MXN billing with CFDI 4.0 invoices. Details are in b2b_needs.
gaps.data_source: N/A (WorkOS / Auth0 for SSO; Facturama / Facturapi or similar PAC for CFDI)

gaps.feature: P1 (employer channel) - Financial wellness content hub beyond investing
gaps.why_valuable: The app assumes the user already invests. Most employees need budgeting, debt management (credit cards, payroll loans), an emergency fund, CETES as a first step, and AFORE basics before stock screeners. Employers buy engagement and measurable completion. Offer modules, checklists and progress tracking, reported to HR only in aggregate.

product.b2b_needs:
What an employer needs before it can give KAIZEN to employees. None of this is possible today: there is one shared password in client code (App.jsx:934), no user or organization model, and all data lives in localStorage (App.jsx:799-815).

1) IDENTITY AND SEATS
- Organization tenants.
- SSO via SAML 2.0 / OIDC (Microsoft Entra ID and Google Workspace cover most Mexican SMEs; WorkOS or Auth0 shorten the build).
- SCIM or CSV provisioning and automatic deprovisioning when an employee leaves; the employee keeps a personal account if they choose to.
- Seat management and invite links.
- Roles: org admin, HR viewer, employee.

2) PRIVACY BY ARCHITECTURE (the selling point)
- The employer must NEVER see an employee's holdings, balances, goals, AFORE data or activity detail.
- The admin console shows only aggregated, anonymized engagement: seats activated, monthly active users, lessons completed, challenge participation.
- Enforce minimum group sizes (for example, no metric shown for groups under 10 people).
- Holdings stored in a user-scoped schema with row-level security, encrypted at rest; admin roles have no read path to it.
- Audit logs; a data processing agreement (DPA) with the employer.
- Under Mexico's LFPDPPP (the new law published March 2025 replaced the 2010 law; the INAI's functions moved to the Secretaría Anticorrupción y Buen Gobierno; confirm current guidance), required pieces include:
  - an aviso de privacidad;
  - express consent for financial/patrimonial data (explicitly required under the previous law's art. 8; verify how the 2025 law treats it);
  - ARCO rights (access, rectification, cancellation, opposition): export and delete.
- A roadmap to SOC 2 or ISO 27001 for larger clients; state the hosting region in the contract.

3) COMPLIANCE COPY AND PRODUCT BOUNDARIES
- Present KAIZEN as education plus analytics, not advice: 'Información educativa; no constituye recomendación ni asesoría de inversión'.
- Remove personalized buy/sell verbs (BUY/SELL App.jsx:378; AGREGAR App.jsx:3458; OPORTUNIDAD backend.py:1623) in favor of transparent rule checklists.
- Personalized recommendations could trigger CNBV rules for asesores en inversiones (LMV arts. 225-227). Have Mexican securities counsel review before selling to employers.
- No order execution and no promotion of specific securities; source attribution on every data point; a risk disclosure page; accessibility (WCAG AA).

4) CONTENT EMPLOYERS ACTUALLY BUY
- Financial wellness beyond stocks: budget, debt (credit cards, payroll loans), emergency fund, CETES as the first investment.
- AFORE: how to check it, voluntary contributions, choosing an AFORE with CONSAR net-return data.
- PPR and deductibility (LISR art. 151-V), taxes in plain Spanish, a risk-profile questionnaire.
- Goals planner in real MXN; short lessons with completion tracking.
- Optional group challenges (paper portfolios, learning streaks) with pseudonymous leaderboards.

5) COMMERCIAL
- Per-seat pricing in MXN. Rough idea only: $49-99 MXN per employee per month, with volume tiers; validate with SME HR buyers.
- Annual contracts and invoicing with CFDI 4.0; B2B buyers in Mexico need a valid factura to deduct the expense.
- Data licensing must allow multi-user commercial display. Vendor terms often price per user or per display, which directly drives seat cost.

6) OPERATIONS
- Uptime SLA; this rules out the Render free tier (render.yaml `plan: free`) and its 60-120 s cold starts (App.jsx:40, 1442).
- Status page, support email/WhatsApp, admin onboarding kit, an HR launch deck, and quarterly engagement reports.
- A mobile PWA, since most employees use phones.
product.data_licensing:
Current state: almost everything comes from yfinance via yft() (backend.py:31 and nearly every endpoint), plus the FRED graph CSV (:516-531, :1824), a CBOE VIX CSV scraped from cdn.cboe.com (:534-548), Stooq for DXY (:550-561), SEC EDGAR (:1044-1177), and RSS feeds from Yahoo, MarketWatch/Dow Jones, CNBC, Seeking Alpha and Investing.com (:779-791).

Risks:
(a) yfinance is an unofficial scraper of Yahoo endpoints. Its documentation says it is intended for research/educational use and points to Yahoo's terms, which limit use to personal, non-commercial purposes. Charging users or giving it to employees is a ToS risk. It is also fragile: Yahoo rate-limits and blocks cloud IPs, which the code already works around with retries, sleeps and fallbacks.
(b) CBOE's website data and Stooq (DXY is an ICE index) have their own terms that restrict commercial redistribution.
(c) On FRED, some series are copyrighted by third parties (e.g. VIXCLS belongs to CBOE; ICE BofA indices). FRED's terms say to respect the original owner's license. Government and OECD series are generally fine with attribution.
(d) Publisher RSS feeds are generally for personal use. Commercial display of headlines needs permission or a licensed news feed.
(e) Showing BMV quotes commercially, even delayed, formally requires a market-data distribution agreement with Grupo BMV. Fees and terms are not public; verify.

FREE, LICENSE-CLEAN SOURCES TO USE NOW:
- Banxico SIE API (free token; attribution). FIX, target rate, TIIE, CETES auctions, UDI, inflation expectations. Series IDs SF43718, SF61745 and SP30578 already appear in Kaizen02 Material/dashboard-arauco/build_snapshot.py:123-125.
- INEGI BIE API (free token; INEGI's free-use terms): INPC, PIB, IGAE, ENOE, release calendar.
- SEC EDGAR (public domain; 10 requests/s with a declared User-Agent, which the backend already sends at :1047-1051): US financials, filings, company_tickers symbol master, insider forms 3/4/5.
- FRED API (free key) for US macro, excluding third-party-copyrighted series.
- CONSAR open data for AFORE returns.
- Ken French data library for US factors.
- BLS and FOMC release calendars.

LICENSED OPTIONS FOR PRICES, FUNDAMENTALS AND CALENDARS. Rough prices from memory as of 2025-26; all uncertain, get written quotes:
- EODHD: 'All-in-One' is about $99.99/mo but for PERSONAL use (Kaizen02 docs/DATA-PROVIDERS.md makes the same point). Commercial display or redistribution needs a separate agreement, price on request. Covers BMV (exchange code MX) end-of-day and delayed data, fundamentals, dividends, splits, earnings and economic calendars, some bonds. Probably the best fit for mixed Mexico + US coverage.
- Financial Modeling Prep: individual plans roughly $20-150/mo. Display or redistribution rights need a commercial/enterprise license (quoted). Strong on US fundamentals and calendars; BMV coverage partial.
- Twelve Data: roughly $29-229+/mo for individuals, higher 'business' tiers for commercial use. Lists Mexican exchange coverage; verify depth.
- Finnhub: free tier; paid modules roughly $50+/mo each; commercial redistribution is a separate contract.
- Polygon.io (reportedly rebranded 'Massive' in 2025): US only; individual about $29-199/mo; business or display plans roughly $2k/mo.
- Alpha Vantage: premium about $50-250/mo; commercial terms on request.

For Mexican fixed-income secondary prices (Bonos M, Udibonos, corporate debt), the official price vendors are Valmer (Grupo BMV) and PiP (Proveedor Integral de Precios): enterprise pricing, likely tens of thousands of MXN per month (uncertain). Start with Banxico auction data instead.

News: Finnhub or Marketaux news tiers (low cost) or enterprise feeds (Dow Jones, LSEG, Benzinga). For Spanish-language coverage, negotiate with El Economista, El Financiero or Expansión, or show headline plus link only after legal review.

Crypto: Bitso public API (MXN pairs, free; check display terms); CoinGecko's free Demo API is non-commercial, paid plans start around $100+/mo.

RECOMMENDED PATH:
- Phase 0, private beta, not charging: keep yfinance, label the app 'beta personal / datos con retraso', add Banxico, INEGI and EDGAR, and stop scraping CBOE and Stooq.
- Phase 1, first paid tier: one commercial vendor contract (EODHD or FMP) with written rights for web display, caching and derived analytics, behind a provider interface (pattern: Kaizen02 src/services/marketData.ts), with source and as-of stored per value. A budget of roughly $300-1,500/mo is plausible but must be quoted.
- Phase 2, employer scale: Grupo BMV distribution agreement for delayed BMV quotes; Valmer or PiP only if a bond-pricing feature needs it.

Unit economics warning: at retail prices of about $99-199 MXN/mo (about $5-10 USD), a $1k/mo data license needs roughly 100-200 paying users just to cover data. Vendor per-user or display fees can dominate B2B seat pricing, so choose the vendor before fixing prices.
product.reuse_from_kaizen02:
Sibling project '02 Kaizen': Vite + React 19 + TypeScript strict, react-router 7, Netlify, English UI. It is a demo-data MVP (README: 'deterministic market snapshot'), so reuse its code patterns, models and content, not its numbers.

1) SEARCH AND NAVIGATION
- src/components/GlobalSearch.tsx: a Cmd/Ctrl+K dialog with global hotkey, focus trap, `inert` on the app root, Escape to close, Enter to open the first result, and navigation to /app/instruments/:symbol. Port it to JSX and feed it from a real symbol master: SEC company_tickers.json (already loaded at backend.py:1057-1070) plus a curated BMV/SIC list with Spanish aliases.
- src/App.tsx:88-123 shows the react-router layout (public shell, auth pages, RequireAuth, /app/* routes). This replaces NEWKAIZEN's useState tabs (App.jsx:1046) and gives deep links.

2) DATA MODEL (src/types.ts)
- Portfolio with benchmark, notes and transactions (:99-109); Transaction (:90-97: buy/sell/deposit/withdrawal). Extend Transaction with dividend, split, fee, fx_rate, tax_withheld.
- Watchlist (:111-115), AlertRule (:148-156), ResearchNote with bull/bear cases, catalysts, risks, citations and thesis status (:117-130), SavedScreen and ScreenerFilters (:132-146).
- UserProfile with goal, markets and asset classes (:27-37).
- MarketProviderStatus with mode, asOf and delayedMinutes (:196-201): exactly the provenance NEWKAIZEN lacks.
- src/lib/storage.ts validState and migrateLegacy: a pattern for safely migrating existing localStorage data.

3) PLANS AND LIMITS
- src/lib/entitlements.ts checkEntitlement(): per-plan caps on portfolios, watchlists, alerts, exports and collaborators, with upgrade messages; usagePercent().
- src/data/demo.ts:23-110 PLAN_DEFINITIONS: Free $0, Individual $19, Professional $49, Team $129 for 5 seats. Useful as a freemium and seat skeleton, but reprice in MXN for Mexico and add an employer tier.

4) COMPLIANCE-FRIENDLY SCORING
- src/lib/policy.ts: screenInstrument() and reviewPortfolio() return pass/watch/fail rules, each with a visible requirement (PEG < 1.5, ROIC > 12%, net debt/EBITDA < 2.5x, max position 20%, max sector 40%). Use this pattern to replace NEWKAIZEN's BUY/SELL (App.jsx:378) and AGREGAR (App.jsx:3458) with transparent 'cumple / no cumple' checklists. Make thresholds user-configurable rather than 'the committee's' numbers.
- sectorWeights() and the Mexico-exposure bar in src/pages/app/PortfolioPages.tsx:33-53 feed directly into the risk and exposure dashboard.
- The same page has a per-portfolio benchmark selector (SPY/QQQ/^MXX) and CSV export (downloadCsv in src/lib/export.ts).
- CAVEAT: analyzePortfolio's diversificationScore, (1-HHI)/(1-1/n) in src/lib/analytics.ts, gives 100/100 to ANY equal-weight portfolio, even two stocks. Use effective N = 1/HHI instead.

5) MACRO AND FX
- netlify/functions/banxico.mjs and fred.mjs: server-side token, series allowlist, date validation, 10 s timeout, cache headers, generic upstream errors. Port the same logic into backend.py.
- Material/dashboard-arauco/build_snapshot.py: Python fetch_banxico() with the Bmx-Token header (:40-90) and a SERIES table (:121-133) including SF43718 (FIX), SF61745 (target rate), SP30578 (INPC y/y) plus FRED series. Same language as NEWKAIZEN's backend, so it drops in almost directly.
- src/pages/app/FxLabPage.tsx plus src/lib/analytics.ts forwardRate() (never throws, returns null) and garmanKohlhagen(): basis for an FX / 'dolarización' lab. CAVEAT: do not port calculateHedgeMetrics(); its effectiveness coefficients (0.52, 0.32) are hard-coded, not estimated.

6) PRODUCT SURFACES TO RE-SKIN IN SPANISH AND WIRE TO REAL DATA
- CalendarsPage with economic/earnings tabs (src/pages/app/MarketsPages.tsx:33-45; demo events only).
- AlertsPage (src/pages/app/UtilityPages.tsx:11-24).
- WatchlistsPage and ResearchPage.
- OnboardingPage (src/pages/auth/AuthPages.tsx:56-62: goal, markets, asset classes); extend it into a perfil de inversionista.
- SettingsPage tabs for profile, appearance, billing, data providers and security.
- HelpPage with keyboard shortcuts.
- Legal pages for privacy, terms, risk and data (src/pages/public/MarketingPages.tsx:34-38).
- The FAQ answer 'Does Kaizen provide investment advice? No…' (src/pages/public/HomePage.tsx:167). Rewrite all of these for Mexican law (LFPDPPP aviso de privacidad, CNBV/LMV disclaimer).

7) PROCESS
- docs/DATA-PROVIDERS.md: the EODHD activation checklist and licensing checkpoint (confirm commercial display, caching and redistribution rights in writing; provenance and as-of on every record).
- The quality gates in CLAUDE.md: Vitest + Playwright + axe, two viewports (1440x900, 390x844), WCAG 2.1 AA in both themes, Lighthouse, and failing e2e on console errors. NEWKAIZEN has zero tests.
- The design-token discipline in src/styles.css (no raw hex values; tokens in both themes). NEWKAIZEN's App.jsx is full of hard-coded colors (e.g. '#374151' at :5364 and :5497, '#135936' at :3195 and :3515) that break dark mode and contrast.
